title: Agent Console
heading: Agent Status
text: Your status controls whether new interactions are routed to you. Status Description Receives interactions :-------- :------------- :---------------------- Available Ready for new interactions Yes Busy At full capacity No Away Temporarily unavailable No Break On a scheduled break No Training In a training session No Login Prep Preparing before going live No Offline Logged out No

title: Agent Console
heading: Status Behavior
text: - If you change your status to Away during an active interaction, a warning appears. - If you don't accept or respond within the configured time, the system automatically sets your status to Away (Idle) . This status isn't available for manual selection. - You can't logout during an active conversation. Transfer or close it first. If your browser closes unexpectedly, active conversations return to the queue after an inactivity threshold. - At the end of a Login Prep period, the system marks you as Away. A pop-up lets you select Mark as Available or Keep Away Status .

title: Agent Console
heading: Status Insights
text: Select View Status Insights from the status icon to see time spent in each status for the current day. For custom date ranges, select View Detailed Status Insights to go to My Dashboard. Administrators configure statuses from Agent Status Management.

title: Agent Console
heading: Real-Time Status Timer
text: When an agent switches to any status, the Agent Status dropdown displays a real-time elapsed timer directly below the status name. This timer represents only the time spent in the current status session, not the cumulative daily total. Timer behavior The timer starts when the agent switches to a new status. The timer resets to 00:00 each time the agent changes status. The timer updates continuously in real time while the agent remains in that status. The timer applies to all statuses, including custom statuses. The timer doesn't affect existing cumulative reporting or the Status Insights view. Timer display The elapsed time appears in DD:HH:MM:SS format (for example, 00:12:34) in the Agent Status dropdown. ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Dark Mode
text: Dark mode switches the Agent Console to a dark color scheme across all screens, backgrounds, buttons, icons, and interactive components. The console saves the preference and applies it across sessions. To turn on dark mode: 1. Select the profile icon at the upper-right corner of the Agent Console. 2. Turn on the Dark Mode toggle. Dark colors configured for Skills or Disposition codes - for example, black - may not be visible in dark mode. Use lighter shades to keep codes readable in both light and dark modes. ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Conversation Statuses
text: Each conversation in the conversation tray displays one of five statuses. The table below describes the meaning of each. Status Meaning :---------------------- :------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Overdue SLA threshold is breached; immediate action is required. Ongoing The agent is actively engaged in a live conversation. Snoozed Conversation is intentionally deferred; a follow-up is scheduled. Idle Conversation is open but awaiting a response. After Call Work (ACW) The agent is completing post-call tasks, such as notes and dispositions. The Conversation Tray displays the following details to help agents distinguish and manage conversations: Status icons — a unique icon per conversation state. Tinted backgrounds — a soft color applied to all non-ongoing conversations. Notifications — a counter for unread customer or system activity. Counts greater than 9 display as 9+. Dynamic elapsed timers — shorthand time display with hover-expanded detail (Overdue status only).

title: Agent Console
heading: Channel Icons
text: Each conversation displays a unique icon for its channel:

title: Agent Console
heading: Color Codes
text: Color Meaning :------ :--------- Blue dot You are actively engaged in the conversation Red dot Conversation is overdue Highlighted entry New email conversation

title: Agent Console
heading: Conversation Timer
text: Each conversation in the Conversation Tray and Live Interaction Pane displays a timer that updates in real time. The administrator configures the timer metric. Metric What It Measures :------------------------- :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Total Chat Handling Time Total duration from when the interaction entered the contact center. Agent Handling Time Time the Agent has spent handling the conversation since accepting it. Agent Last Message Time Elapsed time since the agent sent a message in this conversation. Interaction Handling Time Cumulative agent handling time across all agents, excluding queue wait periods.

title: Agent Console
heading: Search Conversations
text: Use the search bar in the Conversation Tray to find conversations by phone number, email address, or customer name. Matching results appear as you type. Select a result to open that conversation. Search supports all configured languages and returns only active conversations.

title: Agent Console
heading: Customer Sentiment
text: Digital conversations show the customer's real-time sentiment, helping you adjust your approach accordingly.

title: Agent Console
heading: Conversation Information
text: Each entry in the tray shows: - Customer name (if available) - Skills matched to the customer's intent - Last message in the conversation - Customer profile picture - Channel icon - Conversation status icon

title: Agent Console
heading: Manual Call (Dialer)
text: 1. Select the + icon on the Conversation Tray and select Outbound Call . 2. On the Dialer tab, select the country, enter the phone number, and select the transcription language. 3. Select Call . The transcription language dropdown shows your enabled languages and an Autodetect option. If no selection is made, the bot language applies by default. Any language selected are saved for future calls, with the option to modify it before each call.

title: Agent Console
heading: Contacts Directory
text: The Contacts tab shows a public directory published by your administrator. Search by name and select Call to initiate an outbound call.

title: Agent Console
heading: Call History
text: Select + Outbound Call Call History to view: - Name and phone number - Date, time, and call duration - Call type (Incoming, Outgoing, or Transferred) You can only see calls you dialed, received, or had transferred to you. ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Queue Notifications
text: New interactions appear at the bottom-left of the Agent Console with a count indicator.

title: Agent Console
heading: Browser Notifications
text: The system sends browser push notifications for new interactions, even when the console is minimized. Supported browsers: Chrome, Firefox, Chromium-based Edge, and Safari. Each notification also plays a sound. Permit notifications when prompted to receive them. If you block them, you hear the sound alert and see the Next in Queue pop-up.

title: Agent Console
heading: Channel Selection
text: You can choose which interaction types to receive. This option is available only when blended mode is disabled. Option What you receive :-------- :----------------- Voice & Digital (default) All interaction types Digital Chat, SMS, and email only Voice Voice calls only Complete all active interactions before switching channel types.

title: Agent Console
heading: Accepting Interactions
text: Manual Answer Mode Select Accept to take the next interaction. If you don't accept within the configured time, the conversation returns to the queue and your status changes to Away. If Explicit Reject is enabled, you see Accept (✅) and Reject (❌) buttons on each interaction. Rejecting removes it from your queue and returns it for reassignment. In the case of an agent or supervisor transfer, or queue timeout, the transferred conversation appears with a message indicating the transfer source. Auto Answer Mode Interactions are automatically accepted and appear at the top or bottom of the Conversation Tray (based on your sort order) with a New indicator. The indicator clears after you send your first message. If you don't send the first response within the configured time, the conversation returns to the queue and your status changes to Away. When Auto Answer mode is enabled, the Transfer and End buttons don't appear until you send your first message.

title: Agent Console
heading: Understanding Queue Position
text: Each incoming chat interaction displays a Queue Position number that indicates where it stands in line relative to available agent capacity. This number helps you understand the expected wait before a conversation is assigned. What Queue Position Means Queue position 1 doesn't mean a conversation is already being handled. It means that conversation is next in line — either waiting for an agent to accept it, or first in the queue to be assigned when a slot opens. Queue Position What it Means :--- :--- 1 The conversation is immediately next — either held with an agent pending acceptance, or first in queue for the next available slot. 2, 3, ... The conversation is waiting behind others in First In First Out (FIFO) order. How Queue Positions Are Calculated When agents are available, the system fills vacant slots with the first conversations in queue. Those conversations move to an Agent Queue and show position 1 — they are assigned to an agent and awaiting acceptance. Conversations that can't be immediately assigned wait in their respective queues (such as Default or Gold). The first conversation in each queue also shows position 1, because it is next in line the moment a slot opens. Conversations behind it are assigned positions 2, 3, and so on, in FIFO order. Example: Consider 9 chats across queues with 3 available agents (total capacity: 5 slots): Conversations Queue Position Reason :--- :--- :--- :--- 5 chats Agent Queue 1 Immediately assigned to fill 5 vacant agent slots; awaiting acceptance. 1st chat in Default Queue Default 1 First in line; will be assigned when the next slot opens. 1st chat in Gold Queue Gold 1 First in line; will be assigned when the next slot opens. Remaining chats Default / Gold 2, 3 Waiting behind the first chat in their queue, in FIFO order. Multiple conversations can show position 1 at the same time — each across a different queue or agent slot. Position 1 is relative to each queue's or agent's own capacity, not a single global count.

title: Agent Console
heading: Handling Interactions With Filters Applied
text: If a conversation status filter is active (for example, Ongoing or Idle), accepted conversations show a View option until you open the conversation and send the first message.

title: Agent Console
heading: Sorting Interactions
text: 1. Select the ↑↓ icon at the top of the Conversation Tray. 2. Select Latest on Top or Latest at Bottom . ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Live Interaction Pane
text: The Live Interaction Pane is where you communicate with customers.

title: Agent Console
heading: Arrival Summary
text: Every conversation starts with an Arrival Summary when you accept it. It shows: Field Description :------- :------------- Agent Name Your name Summary Conversation summary, including summaries from prior transfers Queue The queue that routed the conversation Wait Time How long the customer waited before you accepted Intent The customer's primary reason for contact Sentiment Customer sentiment based on their messages After you accept, your messages appear below the Arrival Summary. If the bot-customer transcript is missing, a Reload option appears at the top. If sentiment analysis is on but no data is available, the Sentiment field shows "Unavailable."

title: Agent Console
heading: Composing Responses
text: Type in the text editor and select Send , or press Tab + Enter . - Press Enter to send. Use Ctrl+Enter or Shift+Enter (Windows) or Ctrl+Return / Shift+Return (Mac) to add a new line. - Press / in the text editor to open the standard response library. Press Escape to close it. Translation behavior: - When translation is enabled, responses appear in your selected target language. - When translation is disabled, responses appear in the conversation language.

title: Agent Console
heading: AI-Enhanced Compose
text: Use the AI options in the compose bar to improve your draft before sending: Option What it does :-------- :------------- Make more friendly Rephrases the response to be more informal and warm Make more formal Expands the response with formal language Expand Adds more detail to the draft Rephrase Elevates formality for business contexts Enable this from Generative AI Tools GenAI Features Agent Response Rephrasing.

title: Agent Console
heading: Adding Hyperlinks
text: 1. Highlight the text to hyperlink and select the Add Link icon. 2. Select Web Address and enter the URL, or select Email Address and enter the address. 3. Select OK to apply the hyperlink. 4. Hover over the link to access Open , Break Link , or Edit options. 5. Press Enter to send the message.

title: Agent Console
heading: Viewing New Messages
text: If you scroll up during a conversation and a new message arrives, a New Message icon appears at the bottom of the thread showing the unread count. Select it to jump to the latest message.

title: Agent Console
heading: Message Status on Network Disconnect
text: Scenario Result :---------- :-------- Message sent "Sending" appears Message delivered "Sent" appears Network disconnects Chat disabled; undelivered messages show "Not Delivered" with a Resend icon Network restores Chat re-enabled Resend selected Message is sent again If the conversation ends or the page refreshes, the Resend icon no longer appears.

title: Agent Console
heading: Typing Indicator
text: When you type a response during chat, the customer sees three dots indicating you are responding. Requires WebSDK 3.0 with the AgentDesktop plugin installed.

title: Agent Console
heading: Real-Time Sentiment
text: The sentiment indicator (positive, negative, or neutral) reflects the overall sentiment of the full conversation. Select the indicator to view a graph showing emotional fluctuations per message, helping you adjust your tone and approach. Positive: Negative: Neutral:

title: Agent Console
heading: Message Timestamps and Read Status
text: - All agent messages show a date and timestamp. - Consecutive messages sent within the same minute are stacked under one timestamp. - Read status appears against the most recent message in a stack. ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Audio and Video Calls
text: During a chat, you can escalate to an audio or video call by selecting the Audio Call or Video Call icon in the Live Interaction Pane. Video calls require an AudioCodes-enabled account. You must close the chat interaction and the audio/video call separately, each with its own disposition.

title: Agent Console
heading: Call Option Availability in Auto Acceptance Mode
text: For chat conversations assigned in Auto acceptance mode, audio and video call icons are available immediately after the conversation is assigned. An initial text response isn't required before initiating a call. Selecting Audio Call or Video Call accepts the conversation and starts the conversation timer. No additional acceptance action is needed. Existing audio and video call permissions continue to apply. The conversation history, monitoring views, and acceptance metrics reflect call-based acceptance when a call is initiated without a prior text response.

title: Agent Console
heading: Video Call Recording
text: Administrators can enable or disable this feature from System Settings. Prerequisites : Version Requirements for Video Call Recording To use the Video Call Recording feature, ensure both components are running on the minimum supported versions listed below. The feature won't function correctly if either application is on an older version. Component Minimum Required Version :----------- :-------------------------- WebSDK v3/11.23.1 Agent Desktop 11.24.0 WebSDK handles the customer-side of the video call. Update to version v3/11.23.1 or later to ensure customers can connect and their video stream is captured correctly during a recorded session. Agents use the Agent Desktop to initiate the video call and start the recording. Version 11.24.0 or later is required for the recording controls to be available in the agent interface. Both components must meet the minimum version requirement at the same time. Upgrading only one application doesn't enable the feature. Steps to start video call recording: 1. Select Start Video Call Recording to record a video call. The customer receives a consent notification and must select Ok to proceed. If the customer selects Decline Recording, the video call continues without recording. The video call recording notification message displayed in the modal is configurable. The system shows the message in English by default, and the message can be customized. 2. (Optional) To pause recording, turn off the Recording On toggle. Turn it on to resume recording. Use this when collecting PII or PCI data. Recording stops automatically when either party ends the video call. Supervisors can download the recording from the Conversations page.

title: Agent Console
heading: Virtual Backgrounds (Video Calls)
text: During an active video call, open the Virtual Background option to apply a static image or blurred background. The background applies to your video feed only and saves at the browser level for future calls. This feature is in Beta. Contact Support to enable it. Safari isn't recommended for video calls.

title: Agent Console
heading: Agent-to-Customer Screen Sharing
text: 1. Start a video interaction. 2. Select Start Screen Sharing and review the disclaimer. 3. Choose an application window or browser tab to share. 4. To stop, select Stop Screen Sharing or end the interaction.

title: Agent Console
heading: Screen Recording for Voice Calls
text: Agent Screen Recording captures full desktop activity during voice calls using a desktop application. The system stores recordings and provides download access from the Conversations page. Administrators can enable or disable this feature from System Settings. Prerequisites : Install the Windows desktop recording application. Ensure the application runs before accessing the Console. When the agent logs in, the system checks the desktop application through a localhost WebSocket and displays a message with a download option if the application isn't installed. Recording Behavior : Recording starts automatically when the agent accepts a voice call and continues throughout the interaction, including when the call is on hold and during After Call Work (ACW). Recording stops after the agent submits the ACW disposition. Agents can manually pause and resume recording by selecting the Screen Recording icon, for example, while collecting sensitive information. The system excludes any paused duration from the recording. Recording captures the entire desktop across all monitors. Recording includes both the agent's and the caller's audio. There's no maximum duration limit for agent screen recordings. Recordings are stored in WebM format.

title: Agent Console
heading: Agent AI Widget During Video Calls
text: When a chat conversation escalates to a video call within the same interaction session, the Agent AI widget remains active and continues to assist with the video call. What Stays Active Agent AI retains the full session context established during the chat phase, including: Prior chat transcript Customer metadata and case history Detected customer intent Suggested responses and actions Knowledge article recommendations

title: Agent Console
heading: Outbound Calls
text: You can initiate outbound calls from the Conversation Tray. Rules for outbound calls: Condition Can make outbound call? :---------- :------------------------ Any status except System Away or System Busy (Voice) Yes Handling digital interactions Yes System Away (Chat or Voice) No System Busy (Voice) No Currently on an inbound voice call No Currently on an active outbound call No When you start an outbound call, your status automatically changes to System Busy . Steps to make an outbound call: 1. Select + on the Conversation Tray and select Outbound Call . 2. On the Dialer tab, select the number to call from (phone number or SIP trunk). 3. Enter the phone number with the country code and select Call , or select the country from the dropdown, enter the number, and select Call . Dialer behavior: - The ISD code auto adjusts to the last-used country code. - Numbers auto format to a standard format. - Invalid numbers display an error and disable the Call option. - Enable call controls during ringing: Turn on this toggle to use Mute, Hold, Keypad, and Transfer during the dialing phase. Scenario What happens ---------- ------------- Number entered without a country code System places the call directly. Change country to Unknown for US numbers without a code. Pasted number without a country code Validation error appears. Change country to Unknown to proceed. Valid international number (for example, +91987654321) System detects and selects the correct country automatically. Invalid international number (for example, +919876543) Validation error appears; the call button is disabled. The country code defaults to the last dialed country. If no calls have been made, the default is US.

title: Agent Console
heading: Click-to-Call (Inbound)
text: Inbound Click-to-Call interactions appear in the Live Interaction Pane like a standard voice call. The system provides the customer's metadata and prior chat transcript. Available call controls: Mute, Unmute, Hold, Resume, Recording (Pause/Resume), Transcription (Pause/Resume), and Internal Transfer. Supported only in the External SDK.

title: Agent Console
heading: Voicemail
text: If auto-answer mode is on, voicemails appear automatically in your Conversation Tray. If manual mode is on, you receive a notification and must accept the voicemail (no inbound slot is consumed). Once accepted, you can play, transfer, call back, or download the voicemail from the Live Interaction Pane. To call back from a voicemail: 1. Select Call in the VOICEMAIL panel. 2. The outbound dialer opens. Select Call to initiate the call. When a network interruption occurs during a voicemail callback (outbound call), the re-routing behavior follows the same logic as for outbound call interruptions.

title: Agent Console
heading: Consult, Conference, and Warm Transfer (Call)
text: Consult Call A consult call lets you speak privately with another agent while the customer is on hold. 1. Select Transfer , search for an agent, and select Consult . 2. The customer is placed on hold and the consult call connects. The consult call appears in the receiving agent's Conversation Tray. On accepting, the call appears in the receiving agent's Live Interaction Pane. 3. The following options are available to the initiating agent: 4. Use Swap to switch between the customer call and the consulting agent. Switching to the customer call places the consult on hold. 5. After the consult, select Merge to start a conference or Forward for a warm transfer. Consult to a queue: Select a queue during the consult action to route the consult to an available agent in that queue. The system connects to the first available agent based on skills, availability, and capacity. Queue-level consult without selecting an agent: 1. During an active interaction, select External Consult Call . 2. Select a queue. 3. Optionally select a specific agent. 4. Select Queue Consult to initiate the call. The consulting agent must be Available with zero load. A consult can't be started during an ongoing conference, and a conference can't be started during an ongoing consult. Conference Call Select Merge during a consult to bring the customer into the conversation. Up to 4 supervisors and the primary agent can join the same conference call. The conference call appears in the receiving agent's Conversation Tray. On accepting, all parties are connected. - If a participant drops due to network issues, they can Rejoin . - If you leave the call, the supervisor takes full control. - Each participant can transfer the conversation or exit independently. - CSAT links to the last agent who handled the conversation. - All chat transcripts from supervisors appear in yellow. - A notification appears if the customer drops off during the conference call. Warm Transfer After a consult or conference, select Forw

title: Agent Console
heading: Call Transfer (Voice)
text: 1. Select Transfer (or press Alt + Shift + T ) and search for an Agent or Queue . Recent transfer results appear. 2. Search for an Agent or Queue. Transfer to Agent: Select the agent and choose from the available options. Select Transfer to directly transfer the call. Agents with zero Chat/Email slots aren't listed in agent transfers. Transfer to Queue: Select the queue and select Transfer . The system routes to available agents in the selected queue. The queue must be online and, if skill match is enabled, have agents with the required skills. Transfer to External Contact: Your administrator must enable this in Agent Settings. This is a blind transfer-the call ends for you like a normal interaction. Complete ACW after the transfer.

title: Agent Console
heading: Re-routing Voice Calls due to Network Interruption
text: When an agent's network is interrupted, the platform plays a configured message and re-routes the call into the queue at the highest priority for a new agent to handle. Re-routing applies to inbound calls, manual outbound calls, campaign outbound calls, and voicemail callbacks. A conversation can be re-routed a maximum of two times. The maximum queue wait time configuration applies to re-routed calls. Session and routing behavior: The new agent's connection works like a call transfer. The session closes when the customer disconnects or the call ends naturally. If the new agent declines, the call re-enters the queue at the highest priority. If the customer selects Voicemail, Callback, or Consult Call while waiting, that takes precedence and the new agent doesn't receive the re-routing notification. When a new agent is added, a notification displays below the queue; in the original agent experience, when the interruption flow triggers, the active call is removed from their screen and the Console returns to its default state. CSAT attribution: CSAT is attributed to the new agent, consistent with agent transfer scenarios.

title: Agent Console
heading: External Consult During a Live Interaction
text: If you need to consult an external number during an active call: 1. Select the Dialpad icon in the Live Interaction Pane. 2. In the External Consultation Call window, dial the number using one of three methods: - Manual Dialer : Enter the phone number with the country code and select Call . - Contacts Tab : Search for the contact, select Call , then select Call on the dialer tab. - Call History Tab : Select the number from history and select Call to dial. 3. The external call connects and the customer is placed on hold. The Call History tab records all outbound calls. Available controls during an external consult: Mute, Hold, Keypad (DTMF), Merge, Forward, End, Swap. ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Consult, Conference, and Warm Transfer (Chat)
text: Chat Consult, Conference, and Warm Transfer lets agents collaborate before and during a chat transfer, without placing the customer on hold. Consult Chat A Consult Chat lets you exchange messages privately with a target agent while the customer chat remains active. Use it to share context, provide a summary, or seek guidance before transferring the conversation. Steps: 1. During an active chat, select Transfer . 2. In the Transfer widget, search for or select the target agent. 3. Select Consult. An internal agent-to-agent chat session begins. 4. Use the Consult Chat to share context, conversation summary, customer intent, or relevant notes. 5. Switch between the Customer Chat and the Consult Chat using the context-switching control (see Switching Between Chats). The customer chat remains active throughout the consult. The customer isn't placed on hold and isn't notified of the internal session. Switching Between Chats While a Consult Chat is active, human agents can switch between the Customer Chat and the Consult Chat at any time. Switching doesn't interrupt the customer session. No hold or mute action is available. The system preserves the full message history in both threads. Conference Chat After a Consult Chat is active, you can merge the target agent into the customer conversation to create a Conference Chat. Steps: 1. During an active Consult Chat, select Merge . 2. The system adds the target agent to the customer conversation. 3. All three parties-you, the target agent, and the customer-are now part of the same conversation thread. The target agent receives a notification when they're added to the customer conversation. Internal consult messages aren't exposed to the customer. Warm Transfer (Chat) After a Consult Chat or Conference Chat, you can complete a warm transfer by forwarding the conversation to the target agent and exiting. Steps: 1. During an active Consult Chat or Conference Chat, select Forward . 2. The conversation transfers to the target agent.

title: Agent Console
heading: Translate Conversations in Real Time
text: 1. Select Translate on the Live Interaction Pane. 2. Select a language from the dropdown. Select Mark as Default to save it as your default language. 3. The conversation appears in the selected language.

title: Agent Console
heading: Emojis
text: Select the Emoji icon in the compose bar to add emojis to your message.

title: Agent Console
heading: Attachments
text: Select the Attachments icon to share files with the customer. Files are stored in Amazon S3. Files with malicious content (such as embedded HTML scripts) are blocked regardless of file extension.

title: Agent Console
heading: Co-Browse
text: Co-browse lets you view and optionally control a customer's web session in real time. The customer remains in control at all times. Co-browse works only on websites with the Web SDK embedded. Not available on Telegram, WhatsApp, or other non-web channels. Co-browse shows a reconstructed DOM view, not a live screen capture. Starting a co-browse session (Chat or Voice): 1. In the Console, select CoBrowse . Chat: Voice: 2. Select Start CoBrowse . A request is sent to the customer. 3. The customer selects Accept or Reject on the pop-up. Agent toolbar options: Option What it does :-------- :------------- Color Selection Choose annotation colors Annotate Draw or highlight on the customer's screen; use Eraser to undo Request Control Ask permission to navigate the customer's screen Reconnect Re-establish the session after a connectivity issue Release Control Give control back to the customer Customer toolbar options: Option What it does :-------- :------------- Release Control Withdraw agent control at any point Reconnect Re-establish the session Annotate Mark areas on the screen to show you what needs attention Mask/Block Input Hide sensitive fields (passwords, payment details) from you and the logs Co-browse using phone (security code): 1. In the Console, select CoBrowse . 2. Generate a security code and share it with the customer verbally. 3. The customer enters the code on the website. 4. The session starts after the customer enters the code. Co-browse via an external system: When connected through an external system (for example, Genesys): 1. Select Co-browse on the Conversation Tray. 2. Share the generated security code with the customer. The co-browse session starts. Co-browse limitations: - Can't capture native browser dialogs, OS-level UI, other tabs, or desktop applications. - Agent controls are limited to: select, hover, scroll, and HTML form input. - Agent and customer views may occasionally fall out of sync due to DOM-based technology limitations. ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Email Display
text: Emails appear as threaded conversations. Key display features: - Threaded structure -Replies link to the original email chain for seamless context. - Collapsible tiles -Minimize or expand email threads to reduce clutter. - Collapsible thread view -During Reply, Reply All, and Forward, only the latest email shows by default. Select the ellipsis to expand the full thread.

title: Agent Console
heading: Replying to Emails
text: Action Result :-------- :-------- Reply Opens a response window addressed to the most recent sender only Reply All Opens a response window addressed to all participants, including CC recipients Forward Opens a new draft with subject prefixed by Fwd: and all prior attachments included If an email reply fails to deliver, an error notification displays on the console and the message displays a failure icon in the conversation history.

title: Agent Console
heading: Resending Emails
text: 1. Open the email interaction and select Resend . 2. The composer opens with recipient details and original content prefilled. Optionally edit the content. 3. Select Send . The resent email links to the original and is marked Resent in the interaction log.

title: Agent Console
heading: CC and BCC
text: Add recipients in the CC and BCC fields. You can add or remove recipients dynamically and use comma-separated email IDs.

title: Agent Console
heading: Standard Responses in Email
text: From the text editor: 1. Select the Standard Response icon at the bottom of the email editor. 2. Select a category and then the response template. 3. Select the response to use it. 4. Select Send and confirm. From the Responses widget: Select a standard response from the widget. When the editor has content, choose: Option Behavior :-------- :---------- Replace Overwrites the entire editor content with the selected response Append Inserts a line break and adds the response as a new paragraph Copy Available only when the editor is empty For email with a subject field, additional options include Replace with subject and Append with subject . Response template groups and templates appear in the order in which they are configured. To change the display order, see Reorder Response Template Groups

title: Agent Console
heading: Email Delivery Failure
text: If an outbound email fails to deliver due to an SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) timeout, server rejection, or network error, the Console displays an error notification and marks the message in the conversation history. Only the agent who sent the email receives the notification. Other agents and supervisors viewing the conversation see the failure indicator on the message but don't receive the notification. If the failure occurs after the agent navigates away from the conversation, the failure icon displays on the message the next time the conversation loads.

title: Agent Console
heading: Attachments in Email
text: Select the Attachment icon to upload files. Attachments appear as a list. If there are more than three, a View More option appears. Files are stored in Amazon S3.

title: Agent Console
heading: Attachment send failure
text: If a file attachment fails to transmit, the Agent Console displays an error notification and marks the attachment in the conversation history. Only the agent who sent the attachment receives the notification. Other agents and supervisors viewing the conversation see the failure indicator on the attachment but don't receive the notification. ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Notes
text: Add notes for key points, customer feedback, next actions, or suggestions. Previous notes from other agents also appear here. 1. Select Notes . 2. Select + Add New Note . 3. Type the note and select Save .

title: Agent Console
heading: Notes Translation
text: When translation is active, the system translates conversation notes into the selected language.

title: Agent Console
heading: Drafts
text: If you close the email editor with unsaved content, the system saves it as a draft automatically. Drafts persist through logouts and network interruptions. Multiple drafts per email thread are supported. To save a draft intentionally, select X to minimize the editor window.

title: Agent Console
heading: Outbound Email
text: 1. Select + on the Conversation Tray and select New Mail . 2. Enter the recipient's email address, select a queue, and enter the subject and body. 3. Choose an action to send the email, send and open the disposition window (with AI disclaimer if enabled), minimize and save as a draft, or delete the draft after confirmation. The Send or Send & Close option activates only when all required fields (recipient, subject, queue, and body) are filled. Each outbound email consumes one slot from your allocation. The primary send action — Send or Send & Close — is configured by your administrator in System Settings. The non-primary action remains available in the dropdown list.

title: Agent Console
heading: Email Workbin
text: Workbin lets you park an email conversation temporarily, freeing your slot while waiting for a customer reply. Administrators must enable this feature. To park a conversation: Select Workbin in the email interaction header. The conversation leaves your active tray and your slot is released immediately. When the customer replies: - The system attempts to route back to you (the last handling agent). - If you are unavailable, it waits for the configured duration, then routes to the queue. - If no wait behavior is configured, the system applies standard queue routing immediately. Supervisor options while a conversation is in Workbin: - Assign the conversation directly to an agent. - Transfer the conversation to a queue (doesn't wait for you).

title: Agent Console
heading: Personal Workbin View
text: The Personal Workbin View provides agents with a dedicated space to track and manage conversations that are moved to the Workbin. The Personal Workbin View icon is visible in the Console only after an administrator enables the feature. Learn more. Accessing the Personal Workbin Select the Personal Workbin icon in the upper right corner. The view lists all open conversations that are moved to the Workbin and aren't reassigned by a supervisor. If a supervisor reassigns a conversation to another agent, it's removed from your Personal Workbin. What Appears in the Personal Workbin The view displays conversations that meet all of the following conditions: You moved the conversation to the Workbin. The conversation is still open. A supervisor hasn't transferred the conversation to another agent. The columns display Customer (customer name or identifier), Subject (email subject or conversation topic), Date (the date the conversation moved to the Workbin), and Workbin Duration (elapsed time since the last Workbin placement, which resets when the conversation is retrieved and re-parked). Workbin Duration stops counting when the conversation exits the Workbin. Searching Within the Personal Workbin Use the search bar within the Personal Workbin to find conversations. Workbin Duration The Workbin Duration column displays the elapsed time since the conversation was last parked in the Workbin. The timer updates every minute. Select the Workbin Duration column header to sort conversations by how long they have been in the Workbin. Sorting in descending order shows the oldest conversations first, helping to prioritize follow-ups and avoid Turn Around Time (TAT) breaches. Duration format Elapsed time is displayed as DDd:HHh:MMm . Scenario Timer Behavior :-------------------------------------------------- :-------------------------------------------------------------- Conversation moved to the Workbin. The timer starts from the moment the conversation is parked. Conversation retrieved

title: Agent Console
heading: Agent Forms (Secure Forms)
text: Agent forms let customers submit sensitive information securely. When a customer submits a form, the data is masked in your console by default. To share an agent form: 1. Select Agent Form . 2. Select the form and then select Send Form . The form status shows Sent . 3. When the customer submits it, the status changes to Filled . Select the form to view it. 4. Select Unmask to view masked fields (applies only when masking was enabled during form creation). ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Manual PII Redaction
text: During a live chat, you can redact sensitive (PII) data from the conversation transcript. 1. Highlight the text to redact. Select Redact Data . 2. Select Redact Data . 3. Confirm by selecting Redact Data again. The text is permanently masked. - You can select only one user message at a time (multiple lines within that message are permitted). - Available on all digital channels except email. - Doesn't apply to messages in the user's console. ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Snooze
text: Snooze pauses a conversation timer and frees your slot for other conversations while you wait for a customer response or retrieve information. 1. Select Snooze at the top of the Live Interaction window. Snooze is unavailable if the conversation is overdue or you have a reply pending. 2. Select a snooze duration: Today , Tomorrow , Day After , or Custom (up to 30 days in advance). 3. If your administrator has made snooze notes mandatory, add a reason. 4. For a custom duration, turn on the Custom Snooze toggle and set the date and time. 5. Select Apply . A snooze indicator and message appear in the Live Interaction Pane. Hovering over a snoozed conversation in the tray shows the snooze duration and the total count of snoozed conversations. Snooze behavior: - If Agent Logout with Snoozed Interactions is enabled, you can log out and snoozed conversations remain in your inbox for your next login. - If Reactivation on User Message is enabled, a new customer message automatically wakes the conversation. If disabled, you must resume it manually. - If a supervisor transfers a snoozed conversation, it opens when the new agent accepts it. ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Transfer to Another Queue
text: 1. Select Transfer at the top of the Live Interaction Pane, or press Alt + Shift + T . 2. Search for and select a queue. The conversation is transferred. 3. If Skill Modification is enabled, select Next , then add or remove skills. 4. Select Transfer . The system shows only queues within valid hours of operation. If skill match is required, the destination queue must have agents with the needed skills.

title: Agent Console
heading: Transfer to Another Agent
text: 1. Select Transfer or press Alt + Shift + T . 2. Search for and select an available agent. 3. Select Transfer . If the customer ends the chat before the transfer completes, the transfer is dropped and the conversation isn't assigned to any queue or agent. Transfer to External Contact: 1. Select Transfer or press Alt + Shift + T . 2. Search for and select an external contact. 3. Select Transfer . External transfers are blind transfers. The call ends for you like a normal interaction. Complete ACW after the transfer. Administrators must enable this in Agent Settings.

title: Agent Console
heading: Modify Skills Before Transferring
text: If Skill Modification is enabled, you can add or remove skills on the interaction before transferring it to another queue. 1. Select the Add Skills option on the Skills bar. 2. Select or remove skills from the dropdown. ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Ending Interactions
text: 1. Select End in the Live Interaction Pane. 2. Confirm by selecting Yes . The interaction moves to After Call Work (ACW).

title: Agent Console
heading: Timer After Caller Disconnects
text: When a caller disconnects, a depleting timer appears with options to End the call or Call Back . If no action is taken, the call moves to ACW when the timer expires. During a conference call disconnect, the timer shows options to Close or Rejoin .

title: Agent Console
heading: After Call Work (ACW)
text: ACW is the period after a conversation ends during which the agent completes post-interaction tasks like adding notes, updating records, or selecting a disposition. The conversation remains in the conversation tray in ACW status until the agent closes it. ACW Mode Behavior :---------- :---------- Immediate Slot Release Your slot frees immediately. The conversation stays open until you select a disposition and close it manually. No time limit. Timed Slot Release A countdown timer appears. Your slot frees when you submit a disposition or the timer expires. If the timer expires, the system auto fills the disposition. Disabled The conversation disappears immediately. No disposition or notes are required.

title: Agent Console
heading: ACW Duration Timer
text: When a conversation enters ACW state, the Console displays a timer showing how long that conversation has been in ACW. The timer is visible on the conversation in the Conversation Tray and in the live interaction panel. Timer behavior The timer starts when the conversation enters ACW. The timer continues running even if the agent is simultaneously handling other active conversations. The timer stops when the agent closes the conversation. The timer is independent of the agent's status timer.

title: Agent Console
heading: Dispositions
text: A disposition code labels the outcome of an interaction. During the conversation: 1. Select + Add Disposition . The disposition dialog opens with a search bar at the top. 2. Type to search for a disposition by name. Results filter in real time as you type — partial text and any case are supported. Scenario Result :------------------------------ :---------------------------------------------------------------- Type part of a disposition name Matching dispositions appear; non-matching dispositions are hidden. Clear the search field Full disposition list is restored. No dispositions match "No dispositions found" message displays. Keyboard shortcuts in the disposition dialog: Key Action :---------- :---------------------------------- Arrow keys Navigate the filtered results. Enter Select the highlighted disposition. Esc Close the dialog. 3. Select a disposition from the filtered results and select Save . 4. Select End and confirm. The Disposition & Notes window displays. 5. Make changes if needed, then select Close . At the end of the conversation: 1. Select the conversation in your tray. 2. Select a status: Resolved , Abandoned , Pending , or a custom code set by your administrator. 3. Optionally add a description, then select Close . If you don't complete the disposition and notes during the ACW period, the system automatically closes the conversation with a system-generated disposition. Intelligent Disposition Suggestions: If enabled, the system suggests the most appropriate disposition code based on AI analysis of the conversation transcript. Suggestions appear in the disposition bar. Accept with one click or override manually. The Copy option lets you copy the full disposition as plain text. --- Capture Disposition During Transfer When the Capture Disposition During Transfer setting is enabled, agents and supervisors can tag a disposition to an interaction at the point of transfer, before the conversation is closed. To capture a disposition during a transfer: 1. Wh

title: Agent Console
heading: Feedback Surveys
text: After interactions end, the platform can send a feedback survey to the customer. Only one feedback type can be active per channel at a time. Type Scale :------ :------- CSAT 1 (extremely poor) to 5 (extremely good) NPS 0-10 (Detractors: 0-6, Passives: 7-8, Promoters: 9-10) Like or Dislike 1 = Like, 0 = Dislike Select Send Survey in the bottom-right corner of the Live Interaction Pane to include a survey at the end of the interaction. Supported CSAT scenarios (voice): Scenario Trigger :---------- :--------- Inbound and outbound calls End of any standard voice interaction Calls with internal agent transfer After the final agent interaction Calls with agent-initiated callback After the callback interaction completes Calls with internal consult After the interaction ends Conference calls (multiple agents/supervisors) After the interaction concludes Courtesy callback At the end of the callback interaction CSAT doesn't apply when the customer interacts with external agents or when an external consult occurs. To view feedback scores: 1. Go to the Conversations Dashboard. 2. Open the interaction and select the Details tab. 3. If the customer completed a survey, the Feedback field (CSAT/NPS/Like/Dislike) appears. Call Status During Agent-Customer Interaction with CSAT Scenario Condition Status Mode :--------------------------- :------------------------------------------------ :--------- :------------ User hangup before CSAT User disconnects before CSAT is initiated Completed User Hangup User hangup during CSAT User disconnects while CSAT is in progress Completed User Hangup User hangup after CSAT User disconnects after submitting CSAT Completed User Hangup System ends call after CSAT System terminates the call after CSAT submission Completed Agent Hangup ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Request Supervisor Support
text: 1. Select ⋮ (more options) on the Live Interaction Pane and select Request Supervisor Support . 2. Select one or more supervisors from the list. 3. A notification is sent to all selected supervisors with Available status. 4. The supervisor receives the notification. 5. When a supervisor accepts, an Internal Chat window opens for you to communicate with them. ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Agent AI Assist
text: The Agent AI panel provides real-time assistance during conversations. Feature Description :--------- :------------- Agent Bot Shows Next Action suggestions based on the current conversation status Automations Lists pre-configured messages based on customer intent (for example, Welcome, Bill Payment Status) Proactive Suggestions Toggle to enable or disable auto suggestions for the next action ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Responses Widget
text: Use canned responses to send standard messages quickly. Default categories: Category Purpose :---------- :--------- Greeting Welcome messages Conversational Follow-up and delay responses Closing Closing statements, survey requests, thank-you messages Transfer Messages for transferring to a manager or alternate group Abuse Fair and final warning messages for abusive language Privacy Permission-based service responses ---

title: Agent Console
heading: User Info Widget
text: The User Info widget displays customer information for the active conversation. Administrators configure which fields and sections appear, their order, and their visibility. The panel displays only what you configure. Learn more. User Info is divided into three sections: Section What It Shows :-------------------- :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ User Details Key customer attributes such as name, email, intent, country, and city. Recent Visit History A log of the customer's previous visits. Your administrator can turn it on or off. Connection Details Technical session information such as connection start time, source, device, and IP address. Fields within each section appear in the order configured by your administrator. Sections or fields that are turned off aren't displayed. ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Anchor Tags
text: Administrators can configure field values in the User Info widget to render as clickable hyperlinks using a predefined anchor tag syntax. This lets agents open relevant URLs directly from the widget without copying and pasting links manually. Supported Syntax Only the following syntax is supported: link text Component Description :----------- :------------- Link Text The label displayed to the agent as a clickable link. URL The fully qualified URL that opens when the agent selects the link. Example: View Profile This renders as a clickable link labeled View Profile. Selecting it opens https://example.com/customer/12345 in a new browser tab. ---

title: Agent Console
heading: History Widget
text: The History widget displays the customer's previous interactions across all supported channels — Chat, Email, and Voice — in a unified timeline. Use it to review prior context, previous resolutions, and the agents or bots involved before continuing the conversation. Conversations are sorted by Acceptance Time in ascending order, showing the earliest interaction first and the most recent last. Conversation cards Each historical interaction appears as a conversation card. Select a card to open the full transcript. Area What It Displays :------- :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Header Acceptance time and total conversation duration. Body Conversation subject or transfer-triggering intent. For voice or email interactions without a detected intent, the conversation subject or title displays. Metadata Channel icon (Chat, Email, or Voice), bot name if automation handled part of the interaction, and avatars for all agents who participated. Footer Conversation status. Multiple conversation statuses When a conversation has more than one conversation status, the card shows the first two followed by a +N indicator for the remaining count. Select +N to expand and view all conversation statuses. Example: Selecting +2 displays the two additional conversation statuses. Select any conversation card to view the full transcript. Wait time includes the initial queue wait plus any additional waits from agent or queue transfers. Translate historical conversations: 1. Select the History tab and open the conversation. 2. Select Translate on the Live Interaction Pane and choose a language. 3. The conversation appears in the selected language. 4. Select Original to revert to the original language. ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Internal Chat
text: Use Internal Chat to communicate with other agents or supervisors while handling a customer interaction. 1. Select the Internal Chat icon in the upper-right corner of the console. 2. Select an available agent or supervisor from the list. 3. Send messages, attachments, or initiate an internal call. To translate an internal chat: 1. Select Translate . 2. Choose the language and optionally select Mark as Default . The chat translates into the selected language. Administrators can enable or disable translation for internal chats from Translation Configurations. ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Manage Layout
text: Go to Console Manage Layout to add, delete, or switch between layouts. To create a new layout: 1. Select + Create New . The layout page opens with available widgets on the left panel. 2. Drag the required widgets to the layout area. 3. Enter a Layout Name and select Save .

title: Agent Console
heading: External Widgets
text: External widgets in your layout have a Maximize icon. Select it to expand the widget to a full-page view within the console. 1. Select the Maximize icon on an external widget. The widget expands to a full-page view within the console. A disclaimer appears in the original widget tab. 2. Interact with the widget. It automatically refreshes when you switch conversations. 3. Select Close or Minimize to return the widget to its original size. Only one widget can be maximized at a time. Refresh a widget: Select the Refresh icon within a widget to reload its data without refreshing the entire application. ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Notifications
text: Agents can manage how the Agent Console alerts you to incoming interactions and activity. Notification settings cover sound alerts, browser push notifications, and repeat behavior. 1. Select the Bell icon in the upper right corner of the console. 2. Select Settings icon to open the notification preferences. Supported browsers: Chrome, Firefox, and Microsoft Edge. Notifications you can manage: New conversations, customer messages, manager messages, SLA breaches, transfer requests, and error prompts. Select the name on the right to change the sound for a notification type. Error prompt sounds apply only to console runtime errors, not configuration validation errors. Repeat notifications: 1. Select the Repeat icon next to Incoming Interactions to enable it. 2. Set the repeat interval (default: 5 seconds) and click Save . Incoming call sound through speakers when headphones are connected: Enable this option to play incoming call sounds through the system speaker even when a headset is connected. Conversation audio continues through the headset. Enabled: Disabled (default):

title: Agent Console
heading: Queue-specific Sound Profiles
text: Queue-Specific Sound Profiles let you assign a distinct sound notification to one or more queues. When an interaction arrives from a configured queue, it plays the assigned sound instead of the default alert, letting you instantly distinguish high-priority or VIP queues from standard queues by audio cue. This setting applies to voice, chat, and email interactions. How It Works Queues with a sound profile assigned play that sound when an interaction arrives or is transferred to them. Queues without a profile assigned continue to use the default notification sound. If an interaction is transferred and the target queue has a configured sound profile, that sound plays — regardless of whether the transfer occurs before or after you accept the interaction. Configuring a Queue Sound Profile To assign a sound to a queue: 1. Select + Add Queue-Specific Incoming Notification . 2. Search for and select one or more queues. You can select a single queue or multiple queues in the same profile. 3. Select the notification sound to assign. 4. Select the Play icon to preview the selected sound before saving. 5. Select Save . The profile is active immediately. Incoming interactions from the configured queues play the assigned sound. To assign a different sound to additional queues : Repeat the steps above. You can create as many profiles as needed, with no limit on the number of queue mappings. Queues that no longer have a profile return to the default notification sound. Sound Profile Behavior Reference Scenario Sound Played :--------------------------------------------------------- :---------------------------------------- Interaction arrives from a queue with a profile assigned Assigned queue sound Interaction arrives from a queue with no profile assigned Default notification sound Interaction transferred to a queue with a profile assigned Assigned queue sound (before or after acceptance) Interaction transferred to a queue with no profile assigned Default notification sound Profile

title: Agent Console
heading: User Diagnostics
text: Select the User Diagnostics (♡) icon in the top-right corner. - Green icon -Device permissions are active. - Orange icon -Device permissions are missing. A pop-up appears prompting you to enable settings. Select Set Permissions to configure device permissions. Audio Device: 1. Select your Speaker and Microphone from the dropdowns. 2. Select Start Recording to record a clip. 3. Select Stop Recording to stop. 4. Select Play to test the recording. Maximum recording length: 12 minutes. A confirmation appears if no audio issues are detected. Video Device: 1. Select your Camera from the dropdown. 2. Verify the video feed is visible. Connectivity: 1. Select Start Test to run connectivity, bandwidth, and server reachability tests. 2. When complete, view the results. Select Copy Results to share the output. Connectivity tests are available only with a Kore Twilio account. Not supported for SIP trunk setups. ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Connection Handling
text: If your internet connection drops, a message appears at the top of the console. The system attempts to reconnect automatically. If reconnection fails after several attempts, you are prompted to reload the page. ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Proactive Network Monitoring
text: During active calls, the system monitors network performance (packet loss, speed, and MOS score). If metrics exceed the 300 ms threshold, a warning banner appears on the Console. Select Know More to view the last 5 minutes of performance data with the threshold highlighted. Select Report to submit the issue and capture connection logs for analysis. ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Analytics
text: The analytics section shows your daily performance metrics: - Feedback survey scores - Average conversations completed, transferred, and abandoned - Average first response time and average response time ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Agent Profile
text: The Agent Profile gives you access to your personal information, channel settings, and-when permitted-your skill and queue subscriptions. To open it, select the Profile icon at the top right corner of the Console. Section Description :--------- :------------- Profile View and edit personal information. Settings Configure chat and voice experience preferences. Queues and Skills View assigned queues and skills. Modify subscriptions when permissions are enabled. Modify Queues and Skills The Queues and Skills show all queues and skills assigned to you by your supervisor. If your role includes the Modify Skill Subscription or Modify Queue Subscription permissions, you can adjust your routing eligibility. Modifying Skill Subscriptions When the Modify Skill Subscription permission is enabled for your role, you can deselect skills to exclude yourself from routing for those skills at runtime. To deselect a skill: 1. Select the Profile icon to open the Profile slider. 2. Select Modify beside the skills. 3. In the Skills list, deselect the skill you want to opt out of. 4. The skill remains visible but is marked as deselected. To restore a skill subscription: 1. Select the deselected skill to reactivate it, or 2. Select Reset to Default to restore all original skill assignments. Deselecting a skill affects routing eligibility only. It doesn't remove the skill from your profile or affect supervisor-level configuration. Modifying Queue Subscriptions When the Modify Queue Subscription permission is enabled for your role, you can deselect queues to exclude yourself from routing for those queues. To deselect a queue: 1. Select the Profile icon to open the Profile slider. 2. Select Modify beside the queues. 3. In the Queues list, deselect the queue you want to opt out of. 4. The queue remains visible but is marked as deselected. To restore a queue subscription: 1. Select the deselected queue to reactivate it, or 2. Select Reset to Default to restore all original queue assignments. De

title: Agent Console
heading: App Language
text: Choose the display language for the Agent Console: - English (United States) - Japanese (Japan) - Korean (South Korea) 1. Select App Language . 2. Choose your language. 3. Select Save . Language selection doesn't apply to the Platform.

title: Agent Console
heading: Multi-Account Access
text: If you belong to multiple accounts, you can select an account at sign-in and mark one as your default. After signing in, switch between accounts from the top-right corner. ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Help
text: Select the Help icon in the top-right corner to access support resources. - Introduction to AI for Service - Help & Documentation - Community - What's New in v11.x.x - Contact Us - Academy - Submit a Request - Report a voice issue for the current call To report a voice issue: 1. Select Report voice issue for the current call . 2. Select the issue category: Audio Clarity, Connection Problems, Voice Transmission, or Other. 3. Add a description and optionally upload a screenshot. 4. Select Submit . Select Done to close or Download Logs to export logs. ---

title: Agent Console
heading: Related
text: - Routing-How interactions reach agents - Agent AI-Real-time AI assistance - Skills-Agent skill configuration ---

title: Campaigns
text: The Campaigns module enables proactive outreach to customers through voice calls, SMS, and web channels. Use it to create targeted campaigns, manage contact lists, monitor performance, and maintain compliance with calling regulations. Campaigns are available only in the United States (US) and Japan (JP) regions. This feature is turned off by default. To turn on Campaigns for your account, contact Support. To access Campaigns, go to Contact Center AI Campaigns . ---

title: Campaigns
heading: Campaign Types
text: Type Description :------ :------------- Voice Outbound voice calls using agentless, progressive, preview, or power dialers SMS Outbound text messaging using simple or advanced message flows Proactive Web Rule-based engagement widgets (chat, banner, post, or button) displayed on websites ---

title: Campaigns
heading: Campaign Management
text: Go to Contact Center AI Campaigns Proactive Outreach Campaign Management . Enable the Outbound Voice Campaigns permission in User Permissions for agents who handle campaign calls. Agents must be configured for either inbound or outbound — agent blending isn't currently available.

title: Campaigns
heading: Voice Campaigns
text: Campaign Table Column Description :-------- ------------- Name Campaign name and type Actions Play/Pause/Replay, Stop, Edit, Clone Priority 1 (lowest) to 5 (highest); default is 5 Status Ready, Active, Paused, Rerun, or Completed Progress Contact count; refreshes every 5 seconds Contact List The call list being dialed Connection Flow name (agentless) or queue name (progressive/preview) Last Run Date of the last run Last Updated Date of the last update Status definitions: Status Meaning :-------- :--------- Ready Saved and ready to run Active Currently running Paused Temporarily stopped Rerun Restarting after completion Completed All contacts dialed or end date reached The default sort order is by Run Time . You can also sort by Priority : ascending (5→1) or descending (1→5). The Campaigns module requires a Voice Gateway account. If the account uses AudioCodes, or is switched from AudioCodes to Voice Gateway, Campaigns becomes unavailable. Dialer Types Agentless Dialer Automatically dials numbers without a live agent. When a call is answered, it connects to a configured voice experience flow. The dialer detects answering machines, reschedules unsuccessful calls, and generates call metrics. Campaign managers configure the number of simultaneous calls. - Select a Start Flow during campaign creation. - Turn on Answering Machine Detection (AMD) to detect voicemail. - Configure an Automation Node in the start flow for advanced automation. Agentless Campaign Dispositions Agentless Voice campaigns support disposition codes to define call outcomes. You can configure a predefined set of disposition values (for example, Confirmed, Refused, Ignored) and use them for goal tracking and analytics. Configure disposition codes during campaign design by going to Campaigns Proactive Outreach Agentless Dispositions + Add Agentless Disposition. At runtime, the system assigns one disposition per call and stores it in the session tag KoreAgentlessDisposition . The system displays the disp

title: Campaigns
heading: SMS Campaigns
text: Go to Campaign Management SMS . To run SMS campaigns, configure the SMS channel first. Learn more. Campaign Table Column Description :-------- :------------- Campaign Campaign name Actions Play/Pause/Replay, Stop, Edit, Clone Priority 1 (lowest) to 5 (highest); default is 5 Status Ready, Run as Emergency, Active, Paused, Rerun, or Completed Progress Contact count; refreshes every 5 seconds Contact List Lists being messaged Schedule Start and end dates The default sort order is by Run Time . You can also sort by Priority : ascending (5→1) or descending (1→5). Filters Campaign managers can create, save, duplicate, set as default, edit, and delete filters. To create a filter: 1. Select Filters in the top-right corner. 2. Select + Add New Filter . 3. Select Status and Priority with their sub-filters. 4. Select Save & Apply , enter a name (up to 20 characters), and select Save & Apply . 5. Turn on Make this the default view to set it as the default filter. 6. Open the Filters dropdown to view saved filters. Duplicate a filter: Select Duplicate , enter a name, and select Save . Mark as default: Select Mark as Default . Delete a filter: Select Delete , then confirm. Edit a filter: Select Edit , make changes, and select Save & Apply . Create an SMS Campaign 1. Select + New Campaign . 2. Under the General tab, enter: - Campaign Name and Description - Contact Lists , DNC List , and Priority 3. Under the Message tab, select a format: - Simple : For one-way outbound messages. Select a template and edit the message content. - Advanced : For two-way messaging using a start flow with dialog tasks. Supports agent transfers. Editing a template within a campaign doesn't modify the original template. The template selection resets to "None" when edited. 4. Select Save after entering the message. 5. Under Outreach Strategy , select the Caller ID : - Simple format : Shows numbers configured for outbound only, not linked to any flows. - Advanced format : Shows numbers with associated SMS

title: Campaigns
heading: Proactive Web Campaigns
text: Go to Campaign Management Proactive Web . Campaign Table Column Description :-------- :------------- Name Campaign name and type. Actions Play/Pause/Replay, Stop, Edit, Clone. Status Ready, Active, Paused, or Completed. Type Chat, Post, Banner, Button, or QuickChat. Sent Count of proactive messages sent. Goals Count of campaign goals achieved. Filters To create a filter: 1. Select Filters . 2. Select + Add New Filter and choose Web Campaign Type and Status with their sub-filters. 3. Select Save & Apply , enter a name, and select Save & Apply . 4. Turn on Make this the default view to set it as the default. Duplicate a filter: Select Duplicate , enter a name, and select Save . Mark as default: Select Mark as Default . Delete a filter: Select Delete , then confirm. Edit a filter: Select Edit , make changes, and select Save & Apply . Campaign Types Type Description :------ :------------- Chat Pushes a configured message to the chat widget. Banner Displays a banner at the top or bottom of the page. Post Displays a pop-up at the center of the page. Button Displays a button on the left or right side; can be static or action-triggered. QuickChat Displays a chat window, when the campaign conditions are met. Create a Proactive Web Campaign Select + New Campaign , then select the campaign type. Chat 1. Select Chat . 2. Under the General tab, enter Campaign Name and Description . 3. Under Layout Design : - Edit the Message Header (text and optional image). - Enter the message content (supports formatting, links, and variables). - Add buttons with Text , Action (Send to URL / Send to AI Agent / Dismiss), Background Color , and Text Color . - Set Message Bubble Alignment , Bubble Alignment , and Dark Shadow . 4. Under Engagement Strategy , configure: - Website : Add the URLs or page names the campaign applies to. - Rules : Define trigger conditions based on visitor behavior. - Exclusions : Define conditions that prevent the campaign from triggering. - Goals : Define campaign obj

title: Campaigns
heading: Campaign Logs
text: Go to Contact Center AI Campaigns Campaign Management Logs . The Logs page shows all event logs for the current day by default. Column Description -------- ------------- Date & Time Exact timestamp of the event Log Type Campaign type (for example, Proactive Web) Sub Type Event type (for example, Run time) Description Summary in the format: was or to . Reason: . Filters: Use the calendar control to select a date range. Search: Query on the Description field. Enter any part of a campaign name, user name, or reason. Export: Export logs to a CSV file. The export reflects applied filters and search. ---

title: Campaigns
heading: List Management
text: The List Management section consists of essential contact details for the campaigns. There are two subsections: Contact Lists : Contact lists contain vital information about individuals, enabling targeted and effective communication. It's a collection of names and contact numbers necessary for running a campaign. DNC Lists : These are contacts who have opted for Do Not Contact (DNC) or have registered on the national DNC facility, indicating their preference not to receive unsolicited calls. The DNC Lists Contacts count comprises contacts from both uploaded CSV files and contacts added directly through the AI Agent or Human Agent. Go to Contact Center AI Campaigns List Management .

title: Campaigns
heading: Contact List View
text: View all contacts in a contact list from the UI. This view is available for contact lists created using CSV, Passive API, and Subset-based sources. Columns Each contact appears as a row with the following fields, if available: Phone Number, First Name, Last Name, Time Zone, Unique Identifier, and Contact Priority. Use the Column Selector to show or hide fields. Unmapped fields are available but not selected by default. Actions Search -Search by Phone Number, First Name, Last Name, or Unique Identifier (exact match only). Filter -Filter contacts by Priority. Sort -Default sort follows the CSV order or the current database order. Pagination -Displays 50 contacts per page with page navigation. Export -Download the contact list in CSV format. Editing contacts isn't supported in this view. View Contact Lists To view the Contact Lists, select the Contact Lists tab. The contact lists page displays the following details: Column Description -------- ------------- Contact Lists Name of the list Actions Edit and Delete Status Validating, Validated, or Invalid Contacts Total contact count Campaigns Associated campaign names Last Updated Date of last update (default sort) Create a Contact List From Local Drive: 1. title: Campaigns
heading: Proactive Cooldown Time
text: Controls how often proactive widgets appear to the same visitor in a session, preventing campaigns from triggering in rapid succession. Applies per app and per visitor session. Once a visitor sees a campaign widget, no other widget displays until the cooldown period ends-even if the visitor meets the criteria for other campaigns. Only rules met after the cooldown ends are eligible for display. Page Visit Count and other metrics continue to update during cooldown. A campaign template won't display if: - Another campaign template is already active in the browser window - A cooldown period is in effect - The user is in an active chat session - The chat window is open To configure cooldown time: 1. Select Proactive CoolDown Time . 2. Enter a value between 0 and 30,000 (default: 0), and select Save . This setting applies to all proactive campaigns within the application.

title: Campaigns
heading: FAQ
text: What's the difference between resuming a paused campaign and rerunning a completed campaign? Resuming a paused campaign restarts from where it stopped. Rerunning a completed campaign (using the Rerun icon) starts from the beginning of the dial list as a new instance with no data carried over from the previous run. Can two campaigns share the same contact list? Campaigns can share contact lists, but two campaigns can't run simultaneously with the same contact list. How many contact lists can a campaign have? Up to 10 contact lists per campaign. How many DNC lists can a campaign have? One DNC list per campaign. What's the maximum number of contact lists per account? 1,000 contact lists per account. What are the DNC list limits? Each DNC list supports up to 1 million records. Each account supports up to 2 million total DNC records and up to 1,000 DNC lists. How many voice campaigns can run concurrently? Up to 50 voice campaigns at the same time. What are the contact limits? Each account supports up to 5 million contacts. Each contact list supports up to 1 million contacts or a 5 MB file size limit. How does campaign priority work? Priority determines the proportion of contacts dialed across concurrent campaigns. A higher priority value means a greater percentage of contacts are dialed for that campaign. Priority Percentage = (Campaign Priority Value ÷ Sum of All Priority Values) × 100 Scenario Campaign Priority Percentage ---------- ---------- ---------- ------------ Two campaigns Campaign 1 5 62.5% Campaign 2 3 37.5% Equal priority Campaign 1 5 50% Campaign 2 5 50% Can agents transfer calls during outbound campaigns with auto dialers? No. Agents can't transfer calls to another agent or queue during Progressive or Preview campaigns. Can I use the same phone number for both voice and SMS flows? Yes. The voice flow triggers on calls and the SMS flow triggers on text messages to the same number. You can't attach the same number to two flows of the same type. ---
