title: Calibration Sessions
text: Calibration Sessions help QA teams improve scoring consistency by having multiple participants independently evaluate the same customer conversations using the same evaluation form. A Calibration Manager creates the session, selects conversations and the evaluation form, and assigns participants. Participants score conversations independently in Calibration Mode , with peer scores hidden to prevent influence. After submissions, the manager uses Debrief View to compare evaluations, resolve scoring differences, and set Reference Scores . Closing the session generates a shareable Calibration Session Report with agreement results, analyst accuracy, and resolution notes. The experience supports both session management and participant scoring. Calibration Managers can also participate when assigned, while users with QA functionalities access+ can manage their assigned work through Assigned to Me and review completed sessions through Closed .

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Key Capabilities
text: Calibration Sessions provide the following capabilities. Capability Description --- --- Session Configuration Create a session with selected conversations, an evaluation form or scorecard, participants, and session settings. Assign Participants Assign multiple participants to the same conversations so they can evaluate them independently. AutoQA Visibility Configure when AutoQA recommendations are visible during calibration. Calibration Mode Provide a dedicated experience where participants evaluate conversations independently while peer scores remain hidden. Submission Confirmation Allow participants to review and confirm their evaluations before submitting them. Monitor Evaluation Progress Track participant submission and conversation-level scoring progress. Debrief View Compare participant scores side by side and review metric-level scoring differences after all participants submit their evaluations. Scoring Analysis Review metric-level disagreements, participant notes, and AutoQA AI Justification when available. Reference Score Establish the final expected score for a metric after reviewing participant evaluations and debrief discussions. Agreement and Accuracy Measure participant agreement and accuracy using the established Reference Score as the benchmark. Calibration Session Report Review and export calibration outcomes, agreement results, participant accuracy, conversation-level results, and Resolution Notes. Resolution Notes Document decisions and outcomes from the debrief and Reference Score resolution process. Session History Enable Calibration Managers to review closed sessions within their management scope and participants to review sessions in which they participated. Support Participant Coaching Use calibration results to identify scoring inconsistencies and coaching opportunities.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Prerequisites
text: Before creating a Calibration Session, confirm that you have the following: Requirement Description --- --- Quality AI Permissions Require Calibration Manager permission for session management, including creating and managing sessions, accessing management views, debriefing, establishing Reference Scores, resolving scoring differences, and closing sessions. QA functionalities access+ provides access to the participant-facing Calibration experience. Evaluation Form Use a published Human Agent or AI Agent evaluation form that applies to the selected calibration conversations. Conversations Select conversations that match the evaluation form and configured filters. Participants Assign at least two participants to enable scoring comparison. Calibration Scenarios Select conversations that represent the scoring scenarios the team needs to calibrate. AutoQA Evaluation Require available AutoQA evaluation results when the session uses AutoQA recommendations.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Access Calibration Sessions
text: Navigate to Quality AI AutoQA Calibration Sessions . Users see the Calibration experience based on their permissions and session participation: Calibration Managers can access the management experience. Users with QA functionalities access+ can access the participant experience through Assigned to Me and Closed , even without Calibration Manager permission. A Calibration Manager who is also assigned as a participant retains management access and can additionally use Assigned to Me for personal participant assignments. Users without QA functionalities access+ or Calibration Manager permission can't access Calibration Sessions.

Shows only Closed sessions where the user is a listed participant. Displays an empty state when none exist. Create New Session Visible when the user has session-creation permission. Visible when the user has session-creation permission. Not shown. Reference Score Available according to management permissions. Available according to management permissions. Not available. Resolution Notes Available according to management permissions. Available according to management permissions. Not available. Close Session Available according to management permissions. Available according to management permissions. Not available. Debrief View Available according to debrief rules. Available according to debrief rules. Not available. title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Roles and Participation
text: Permissions determine which parts of Calibration a user can access. Session participation determines whether the user receives participant-specific scoring access. User Type Available Experience --- --- Calibration Manager — not a participant All , Active , and management-scoped Closed views. Can create, monitor, debrief, resolve, and close sessions according to available permissions. Calibration Manager — also a participant All management capabilities plus Assigned to Me , personal scoring progress, and Score Now for participant assignments. QA functionalities access+ without Calibration Manager permission Assigned to Me for Active sessions in which the user participates and Closed for sessions in which the user participated. QA functionalities access+ with no current assignment Assigned to Me remains visible and displays the appropriate empty state.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Calibration Sessions Landing Page
text: The Calibration Sessions landing page provides access to calibration sessions based on the user's permissions and participation. - When no calibration sessions exist, All displays: No Calibration Sessions — Create a session to start calibrating auditor scoring. - Use Search to find a session by name. - Select + Create New Session to create a session when available. - The page includes four tabs: All , Active , Closed , and Assigned to Me .

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: All
text: The All tab displays calibration sessions within the user's available scope. Column Description --- --- Name Displays the calibration session name. Conversations Displays the number of conversations included in the session. Auditors Displays assigned participants as an avatar stack. Created Displays the session creation date. Status Displays the session status: Draft, Active, or Closed. Agreement Displays the session agreement rate when available. Actions Provides actions based on the session status and user's permissions. Available Actions - View: Opens session details or reports. Active and Closed sessions open in read-only or monitoring mode. - Edit: Available for Draft sessions to continue configuration. - Draft Actions: Cancel , Save as Draft , and Next are available during Draft configuration.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Active
text: The Active tab is available to Calibration Managers and displays Active sessions within their management scope. Opening an Active session enables the manager to monitor participant progress, review scoring activity, access Debrief View , resolve scoring differences, and close the session. The Active tab lists calibration sessions that are in progress. Column Description --- --- Name Displays the calibration session name. Conversations Displays the number of conversations included in the session. Auditors Displays assigned participants as an avatar stack. Created Displays the session creation date. Status Displays the current session status: Active. Agreement Displays the current agreement rate when available. Actions Provides actions available for the Active session based on the user's permissions. Available Actions - View: Opens the Active session in read-only or monitoring mode to review current calibration results and progress. - Session Management Actions: Provides additional actions based on the user's permissions. Active Session View When a user opens an Active session, the page displays: - Session Details: Session name, conversation count, auditor count, creation date, conducted-by user, and current status. - Submission Progress: Overall submitted evaluations and each auditor's scoring progress. - Conversation-Level Summary: Conversation details, including: - Handled By: Agent associated with the conversation. - Flow or Queue: Flow or queue associated with the conversation. - Conversation ID: Unique conversation identifier. - Date: Conversation date. - Duration: Conversation duration. - AutoQA Score: Automated quality-assurance score. Session Views Status View --- --- Draft Displays General, Select Conversations, and Assign Auditors, along with conversation filters and configuration actions. Active Displays Agreement Breakdown, Metric Calibration Gaps, Conversation-Level Summary, and Consensus Alignment Summary. Closed Displays the final Calibration Session R

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Closed
text: The Closed tab provides access to completed calibration sessions based on the user's permissions. User Type Closed Tab Scope --- --- Calibration Manager Closed sessions within the manager's management scope, regardless of participation. Calibration Manager + Participant Closed sessions within the manager's management scope. Participation doesn't restrict the management view. Non-Manager Participant Only Closed sessions in which the user participated. Participant Closed View For participant-facing users, each session displays: Field Description --- --- Session Name Displays the calibration session name. Conducted By Displays the Calibration Manager who created the session. Date Closed Displays the date the manager closed the session. Conversations Displays the number of conversations included in the session. Auditors Displays assigned participants as an avatar stack. Agreement Rate Displays the final agreement rate. Select View Report to open the read-only Calibration Session Report. When no applicable sessions exist, the tab displays: No closed calibration sessions yet.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Assigned to Me
text: The Assigned to Me tab provides the participant entry point for calibration scoring. It's available to Calibration Managers assigned as participants and to users with QA functionalities access+ . For users without Calibration Manager permission, the tab remains visible even when no sessions are assigned. Assigned to Me displays only Active calibration sessions in which the logged-in user participates. It excludes Draft sessions, Closed sessions, and sessions the user manages without participating.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Session Details
text: Each session displays: Field Description --- --- Session Name Displays the calibration session name. Created By Displays the Calibration Manager who created the session. Scoring Progress Displays the participant's progress as X of Y conversations scored. Personal Status Displays Not Started (grey), In Progress (blue), or Submitted (green) based on the participant's own scoring status.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Available Actions
text: - View: Opens the participant's assigned conversations. - Score Now: Opens the first unscored conversation in Calibration Mode . - Submitted: When the participant submits all assigned evaluations, Score Now changes to an inactive Submitted state. Assigned to Me doesn't provide management actions such as Debrief View , Reference Score , Resolution Notes , or Close Session .

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Calibration View
text: The participant's view displays: Handled By, Flows/Queues, Conversation ID, Duration, AutoQA Score, Status, and Score Now.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Score Now
text: Each conversation card displays Score Now when the participant has conversations remaining to score. Selecting Score Now opens the corresponding conversation in Calibration Mode . After the participant submits all assigned evaluations, the action changes to an inactive Submitted state. Calibration Mode keeps participant scores hidden from other participants during scoring. When the user has no Active sessions assigned, display: No calibration sessions are assigned to you yet .

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Session Status
text: Status Description ---------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------- Draft The manager has started configuring the session but hasn't activated it. Active The session is in progress and assigned evaluations remain incomplete. Closed The manager has completed the calibration review and closed the session.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Calibration Session Workflows
text: Calibration Sessions help QA teams identify and resolve scoring differences by having multiple participants independently evaluate the same conversations. The experience supports two complementary workflows:

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Management Workflow
text: The Calibration Manager creates and configures the session, selects the conversations and evaluation form, and assigns participants. After participants submit their evaluations, the manager uses Debrief View to compare scores, review disagreements, establish Reference Scores , add Resolution Notes , and close the session.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Participant Workflow
text: Participants with QA functionalities access+ access the Calibration experience through Assigned to Me and Closed . Assigned to Me provides access to their assigned Active sessions, where they score conversations in Calibration Mode , track personal progress, and submit evaluations. Calibration Mode keeps peer participant scores hidden during scoring. After the manager closes the session, participants can access Closed and select View Report to review the read-only Calibration Session Report . A Calibration Manager assigned as a participant can perform both workflows.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Create a Calibration Session
text: Select + Create New Session to start a calibration exercise. The wizard has three steps: General , Select Conversations , and Assign Auditors . A Calibration Manager creates a session by configuring the session, selecting conversations, and assigning QA Analysts. After the manager activates the session, assigned analysts receive the calibration work in their audit queue.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Step 1: General
text: Define the session configuration. 1. Enter a Name for the calibration exercise. 2. Enter a Description with instructions or context for participating analysts. 3. Turn on Analyst Justification Mandatory when participants must add a comment before submitting a metric score. 4. Select an AutoQA Visibility option. 5. Select the Evaluation Form participants use to score the conversations. 6. Select Next , or Save as Draft to continue later.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: AutoQA Visibility
text: The Calibration Manager can control when analysts see AutoQA recommendations during calibration. The available options are: Option Description -------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Hidden until all analysts submit AutoQA recommendations remain hidden until every assigned analyst submits the session. Visible throughout AutoQA recommendations remain visible during the complete evaluation. Visible after each analyst submits AutoQA recommendations become visible only after an individual analyst submits the evaluation.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Step 2: Select Conversations
text: Select the conversations for participants to evaluate. 1. Select a Conversation Type to define which conversations are available to add. - Audited : Displays audited conversations that are already audited. - Unaudited : Displays conversations that aren't audited. 2. Select a conversation source tab: All Conversations: Conversations that match the selected filters. Marked for Calibration: Conversations that analysts or supervisors previously flagged using Mark for Calibration on the audit screen. See Mark a Conversation for Calibration. 3. Use the Search field to find specific conversations. 4. Select Filter to narrow the list of available conversations. 5. Configure the required filters and select Apply . 6. Select individual conversations or Select all . 8. Select Add Interactions to add it to the Selected Conversations panel. 9. Select View Conversation to preview a conversation, or remove a conversation from the selection. Select at least one conversation to proceed. 10. Select Next . Each selected conversation displays: Conversation ID , Flows or Queues , Duration , Sentiment Score , and AutoQA Score . Audit Screen Navigation : Mark for Calibration is available from the Ellipsis (⋮) menu on the Audit screen. After the action is successfully completed, the option becomes disabled. Conversation Filters The filter panel helps narrow conversations before adding them to the session. Filter Description ------------------- --------------------------------------------------------- Date Range Filters conversations using evaluation date. Evaluation Form Displays conversations evaluated with the selected form. Queues Filters conversations by queue or experience flow. Agents Filters conversations by evaluated agents. Duration Filters conversations using minimum and maximum duration. AutoQA Score Filters conversations using an AutoQA score range. Sentiment Score Filters conversations using a sentiment score range. Select Apply to apply the filter. Mark a Conversation for Cal

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Step 3: Assign Auditors
text: Assign the QA Analysts who can evaluate every selected conversation independently. 1. Use Search Auditors to Add to find participants. 2. Select one or more participants. 3. Review the selected participants listed in the Auditors section. 4. Select Create and Notify Participants to activate the session. 5. Alternatively, select Save as Draft to continue configuring the session later. 6. Select Save to save the current configuration. Each participant receives the same set of selected conversations and evaluates them independently. A Calibration Session requires at least two participants. Selecting Create and Notify Participants changes the session status to Active and sends an email notification to the assigned participants.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Monitor an Active Session
text: Opening an active session from the landing page displays the manager's monitoring view. The session header displays the Created Date , Auditors avatar stack, Conducted by , and Status .

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Submission Progress
text: Submission Progress displays the overall participant submission status and individual participant progress. Each participant card displays the participant's name, number of Conversations Scored , and a progress bar. A participant card reaches 100% and turns green when all assigned conversations are submitted.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Conversation-Level Summary
text: The Conversation-Level Summary lists the conversations included in the session. Column Description ------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Handled By Identifies the agent who handled the conversation. Flows/Queues Displays the Experience Flow for conversations handled by an AI Agent and the queue for conversations handled by a Human Agent. Conversation ID Identifies the conversation. Date Displays the conversation date. Duration Displays the conversation duration. AutoQA Score Displays the AutoQA score when available. If the logged-in manager is a participant, Score Now is available for the manager's pending participant assignments. For more details, see Manager as Participant. The Flows or Queues column displays the Experience Flow for conversations handled by an AI Agent , and the queue for conversations handled by a Human Agent .

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Calibration Evaluation
text: Calibration Mode is the scoring experience for QA Analysts participating in a Calibration Session. It uses the selected evaluation form and keeps peer scores hidden so analysts can independently evaluate each conversation. A Calibration Mode indicator identifies that the analyst is completing a calibration evaluation rather than a production audit. During calibration: Peer scores remain hidden. AutoQA visibility follows the session's configured AutoQA Visibility setting. Analysts evaluate each metric independently. Add comments when Analyst Justification has the Mandatory option enabled. Audit Progress displays evaluation completion status. Analysts can't modify an evaluation after submission. Calibration Session conversations aren't routed to the agent for review, acknowledgement, or dispute.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Complete a Calibration Evaluation
text: 1. Open an assigned Calibration Session. 2. Select a pending conversation. 3. Review the conversation transcript. 4. Evaluate each metric using the selected evaluation form. 5. Add notes to provide additional scoring context. 6. Review the completed evaluation. 7. Confirm that the evaluation is final. 8. Select Submit Score . After submission, the evaluation becomes final. The analyst can't modify it unless a separate correction workflow is available. Submitted calibration scores don't affect agent dashboards, leaderboard rankings, or scorecard scores.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Calibration Mode Options
text: Participants can: - Review the Agent and Audit Review details. - View Audit Progress . - Bookmark the conversation. - Cancel scoring. - Submit Score. Scores submitted in Calibration Mode apply only to the calibration session.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Manager as Participant
text: When a Calibration Manager participates in a session, the manager can use Assigned to Me and Score Now to complete their participant evaluation while retaining management capabilities. The manager's participant status operates independently of other participants. After the manager submits their evaluation, Open Debrief becomes available according to the applicable debrief rules. The manager can access Open Debrief without waiting for other participant assignments to change. Available Actions - View: Opens the read-only Calibration Session Report. - Export CSV: Exports available calibration results. Session Report The Closed session report includes: Agreement Breakdown , Metric Calibration Gaps , Conversation-Level Summary , Consensus Alignment Summary , Conversation-level comparison details , and Final calibration results . For more information, see Calibration Session Report. Audit Allocations as a Secondary Access Path Existing Calibration access in Audit Allocations remains available to eligible users as a secondary path to calibration work. Assigned to Me remains the primary entry point for participant scoring. Existing Calibration Access Existing calibration sessions, scoring records, reports, and agreement calculations remain unchanged. A Calibration Manager who does not participate continues to use All , Active , and Closed management views. Capability Access Summary Capability Calibration Manager Manager + Participant QA functionalities access+ only --- --- --- --- Assigned to Me Only when participating Yes, for personal assignments Yes All Yes Yes No Active Yes Yes No Closed Management scope Management scope Participated sessions only Create New Session When creation permission is available When creation permission is available No Score Now Only for personal assignments Yes, for personal assignments Yes Debrief View Yes, subject to debrief rules Yes, subject to debrief rules No Reference Score Yes Yes No Resolution Notes Yes Yes No Close Session Yes Yes No

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Debrief View
text: Debrief View is a management function that allows the Calibration Manager to compare participant evaluations and resolve scoring differences. Debrief View is available only to Calibration Managers according to the applicable debrief rules. It is not available to non-manager participants. For a Calibration Manager who is also a session participant, Open Debrief becomes available after the manager submits their own participant evaluation, according to the applicable debrief rules. The manager can then review participant evaluations, compare scoring differences, and establish the Reference Score. Debrief View is available only to Calibration Managers and isn’t available to non-manager participants. The view opens from a conversation in the session and provides a metric-by-metric comparison of participant evaluations. Depending on the available data, the comparison can include: Participant Scores, Participant Notes, AutoQA information (when available), Reference Score, Resolution Notes, and Accuracy, when Reference Scores are available. The Calibration Session Report uses the same comparison grid structure when the manager selects View for a conversation in the Conversation-Level Summary .

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Debrief View Components
text: Component Description --- --- Conversation Identifies the conversation under review. Each conversation appears as a tab with Handled By , Flow / Queue , Agreement Rate , and Most Disputed Metric . Metric Displays the evaluation metric under comparison. Participant Scores Displays each participant's response for the metric in a separate column with a checkmark, cross, or N/A indicator. Agreement Rate Displays the agreement result for the metric. AutoQA Verdict Displays the AutoQA result when available. Participant Notes Displays notes entered by participants. AutoQA AI Justification Displays the AutoQA explanation for the metric when available. Accuracy Displays accuracy based on the established Reference Score when available. Reference Score Records the manager's final score for the metric. Resolution Notes Records the manager's explanation for the final resolution. The Participant Summary displays participant scoring and alignment information when available. For example, for the Resolution Effectiveness metric, the comparison grid displays each participant's Adhered , Not Adhered , or N/A response, the AutoQA Verdict when available, and the metric's Agreement Rate . At the bottom of Debrief View , the Participant Summary displays Metrics Scored , Aligned with Consensus (%) , and Accuracy for each participant.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Review a Disagreement
text: 1. Open Debrief View after all required participant evaluations are submitted. 1. Select a conversation. 1. Review participant scores for each metric. 1. Identify metrics where the scores differ. 1. Review participant notes and AutoQA AI Justification , when available. 1. Determine the appropriate Reference Score. 1. Add Resolution Notes explaining the decision. 1. Resolve all required disagreements before proceeding. 1. Review the final calibration results.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Reference Score
text: The Reference Score is the Calibration Manager's final determination for a metric after reviewing participant evaluations and supporting evidence. It represents the expected scoring outcome for the calibration exercise and is used to calculate individual participant accuracy.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Close a Calibration Session
text: The Calibration Manager closes the session after completing the required calibration review. Before closing the session, the manager should: 1. Review all analyst scores. 2. Resolve the required scoring differences. 3. Set Reference Scores . 4. Add Resolution Notes . 5. Review the calibration results. 6. Close the session. After the session Is closed: - The session status changes to Closed. - Final calibration results become available. - Participants can access the read-only Calibration Session Report from the Closed session. - Calibration Managers can access the report for sessions within their management scope.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Calibration Session Report
text: Closing a session generates a read-only Calibration Session Report , which is available to the Calibration Manager and all participating QA Analysts. The report summarizes calibration outcomes, analyst alignment, scoring consistency, and areas that require additional calibration. The report header displays the session name , date closed , conducted by , participants , and conversation count .

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Report Sections
text: Section Description ------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Agreement Breakdown Displays the distribution of Full Agreement , Partial Agreement , and No Agreement results, along with the Overall Agreement Rate for the session. Metric Calibration Gaps Lists evaluation metrics ranked by agreement rate, from lowest to highest, and identifies metrics that may require additional calibration. Conversation-Level Summary Displays each conversation included in the session, along with its agreement results and the most disputed metric. Select the View icon to expand a conversation and review detailed metric-level comparisons. Consensus Alignment Summary Displays per-analyst results for Parameters Evaluated, Consensus Alignment, Inter-Auditor Agreement, and Accuracy. An AutoQA benchmark row appears below the analyst rows and compares AutoQA results with human consensus without including them in the consensus calculation.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Conversation-Level Comparison
text: Select the view icon on a Conversation-Level Summary row to expand the row inline and reveal the metric-by-analyst comparison grid directly beneath it, without leaving the report. This expanded grid uses the same structure as Debrief View. Accuracy In the reviewed report data, Accuracy measures how well an analyst's scores match the final Reference Scores established by the Calibration Manager during Debrief. For example, if an analyst's scores match the Reference Scores for 8 out of 10 metrics , their accuracy is 80% . If the Calibration Manager hasn't established Reference Scores, the report can't calculate Accuracy.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Export the Report
text: Select Export CSV to download the calibration results as a CSV file.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Exported CSV Fields
text: The exported CSV contains calibration results from the report. Field Description --- --- Session Details Calibration session name and relevant session information. Conversation Conversations included in the calibration session. Analyst Scores Scores submitted by participating QA Analysts. Reference Scores Final scores established by the Calibration Manager during Debrief. Agreement Rate Agreement result for the calibration session. Per-Analyst Accuracy Accuracy of each analyst compared with the established reference score. Resolution Notes Manager's explanation for resolved scoring differences. Calibration Outcome Final results of the calibration exercise. Participants can use the report to compare their evaluations with the final Reference Scores and review Resolution Notes for resolved scoring differences. When AutoQA results are available, the report also compares them with human consensus to show how closely AutoQA aligns with human evaluators.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Calibration Results and Formulas
text: The system calculates calibration results after participant evaluations are available and Reference Scores are established where required.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Variables
text: Use distinct variables to avoid ambiguity. Variable Definition --- --- N Number of human participants in the session. C Number of conversations in the session. M Number of metrics evaluated per conversation. A Number of Adhered responses for a metric. B Number of Not Adhered responses for a metric. D Number of N/A responses for a metric. For each metric: A + B + D = N

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Metric Agreement Rate
text: A metric reaches consensus when more than half of the participants select the same verdict. If no verdict receives more than N / 2 responses, classify the metric as No Consensus . For metrics with consensus: $$ \text{count} N / 2 $$ Otherwise, the system labels the metric No Consensus and excludes it from further calculations. $$ \text{Metric Agreement Rate} = \frac{\max(A, B, C)}{N} $$ The system computes the Metric Agreement Rate only when the metric reaches consensus.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Session Agreement Rate
text: The Session Agreement Rate averages the agreement rates for all metrics that reach consensus. The system excludes metrics labeled No Consensus. sum of all metric agreement rates / number of consensus metrics $$ \text{Session Agreement Rate} = \frac{\text{sum of all metric agreement rates}}{\text{number of consensus metrics}} $$

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Agreement Distribution
text: The system groups metrics into the following agreement categories: Category Condition ---------------------- ----------------------------------------------------- Full Agreement Metric Agreement Rate = 100% Majority Agreement Metric Agreement Rate is between 50% and 100% No Consensus No verdict receives more than N / 2 responses.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Session N/A Rate
text: The Session N/A Rate measures the proportion of metric responses that analysts marked N/A. $$ \text{Session N/A Rate} = \frac{\text{total N/A verdicts across all metrics}}{C \times M \times N} $$

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Auditor Agreement Rate (Aligned with Consensus)
text: For each analyst, the proportion of their verdicts that matched the consensus verdict, excluding No Consensus metrics from both the numerator and denominator. $$ \text{Auditor Agreement Rate} = \frac{\text{number of matching verdicts}}{\text{number of consensus metrics}} $$

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Auditor N/A Rate
text: The Auditor N/A Rate measures the proportion of metrics for which an analyst selected N/A . $$ \text{Auditor N/A Rate} = \frac{\text{metrics where the analyst responded N/A}}{C \times M} $$ The Participant Summary flags an analyst when their N/A rate exceeds the session average by more than 15 percentage points.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Auditor Inter-Auditor Agreement (Cohen's Kappa)
text: Measures whether an analyst's alignment with the group consensus reflects genuine agreement rather than shared scoring bias, using the three verdict categories ( Adhered , Not Adhered , and N/A ). Where: P o = the analyst's Auditor Agreement Rate. P chance = the probability the analyst and the consensus would match by chance, using each side's verdict distribution. $$ \text{Kappa} = \frac{\text{P\ o} - \text{P\ chance}}{1 - \text{P\ chance}} $$ The report displays Kappa only when the analyst scored 10 or more consensus metrics, and shows a dash otherwise.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Kappa Interpretation
text: Kappa Range Interpretation ------------- -------------- Below 0.4 Poor 0.4–0.6 Moderate 0.6–0.8 Substantial Above 0.8 Near-perfect

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Per-Conversation Agreement Rate
text: The Conversation-Level Summary calculates the agreement rate for each conversation using the same method as the Session Agreement Rate , scoped to that conversation.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Per-Analyst Accuracy
text: A recommended calculation for individual analyst accuracy is: $$ \text{Analyst Accuracy (\%)} = \frac{\text{Number of metrics matching the Reference Score}}{\text{Total metrics evaluated by the analyst}} \times 100 $$ For example, if an analyst's scores match the Reference Score for 42 of 50 metrics: $$ \text{Analyst Accuracy} = \frac{42}{50} \times 100 = 84\% $$ This result helps the Calibration Manager identify analysts who consistently score differently from the established team standard.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Most Contested Metric
text: The Most Contested Metric is the metric with the lowest agreement rate, shown per conversation and at the session level. When two metrics share the lowest rate, the report displays the one that appears first in the evaluation form.

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Metric Calibration Gaps — Thresholds
text: The Metric Calibration Gaps panel sorts metrics ascending by agreement rate, lowest first, and applies these thresholds across the Calibration module. Label Agreement Rate Color ------------------------ -------------- ----- Calibrated 80% or above Green Needs Attention 65–79% Amber Calibration Required Below 65% Red

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: AutoQA in Calibration Calculations
text: AutoQA appears in the Consensus Alignment Summary as a reference row. It isn't included in consensus or agreement calculations based on human analyst verdicts. Consensus calculation : Human analyst verdicts determine consensus. The system excludes the AutoQA verdict from N and the A , B , and C counts. AutoQA Consensus Alignment : Uses the Auditor Agreement Rate formula and treats AutoQA as an additional participant. The system compares its verdict with the human-only consensus. AutoQA Cohen's Kappa: Computed using the Auditor Kappa formula, treating AutoQA as an additional analyst, with the consensus distribution drawn from human analysts only. The report displays the AutoQA row below the human analyst rows with the following note: AutoQA evaluated against human consensus; not included in consensus calculation .

title: Calibration Sessions
heading: Calibration Session Lifecycle
text: A Calibration Session follows a structured workflow from setup to reporting. Stage Calibration Manager Participant --- --- --- Draft Creates and configures the session. Can't access the session for scoring. Activate Assigns participants and activates the session. Receives the assignment and email notification. Score Monitors progress and, when assigned as a participant, scores personal conversations. Scores assigned conversations in Calibration Mode. Submit Waits for all required submissions. Completes and submits the evaluation. Debrief Compares scores and reviews disagreements. — Resolve Sets Reference Scores and Resolution Notes. — Results Reviews agreement and participant accuracy. — Close Closes the session and generates the report. — Report Reviews the final report. Reviews the final report after closure. When a Calibration Manager participates in a session, the manager follows the same Score and Submit stages as other participants while continuing management responsibilities. See Manager as Participant. Each stage helps the Calibration Manager configure the session, collect independent participant evaluations, compare scoring differences, establish Reference Scores, and review final calibration results.

title: Audit Allocations
text: Audit Allocations is a centralized workspace for QA Managers, Supervisors, Auditors, and Operations Heads to create, assign, track, and manage manual evaluations throughout the audit lifecycle. It provides a guided workflow to define the evaluation scope, allocate interactions, distribute workloads, monitor progress, and manage disputes. Allocation behavior is determined by the evaluation form configuration: - Experience Flow assignments create AI Agent allocations. - Queue assignments create Human Agent allocations. - Support of assigning an evaluation form to either Experience Flows or Queues, but not both. Experience Flow-based allocations evaluate AI Agent conversations, while queue-based allocations use queues, agents, and agent groups to evaluate Human Agent conversations. Audit Allocations supports voice and chat interactions, multiple languages, workload reassignment, and role-based workspaces for allocations, assigned audits, auditor performance, personal evaluations, disputes, and resolved audits. Note: The Minimum Duration Threshold applies only to new conversations from Native CCAI, Agent AI, and Quality AI Express sources. It also applies to AI Agent conversation segments evaluated with Experience Flow-based evaluation forms. Only conversations and conversation segments that meet the threshold are included in evaluation and analytics. ---

title: Audit Allocations
heading: Key Capabilities
text: - Create audit allocations for Human Agent and AI Agent conversations. - Support Experience Flow-based AI Agent allocations and Queue , Agent , and Agent Group-based Human Agent allocations. - Allocate interactions using Random or Custom allocation methods with quick or saved filters. - Distribute interactions using percentage-based or fixed-count allocation. - Apply minimum duration thresholds to exclude ineligible interactions. - Support multiple auditors for Human Agent evaluations. - Reassign pending interactions without affecting completed evaluations. - Monitor allocation progress, auditor workload, completion rates, pending audits, and average audit scores. - Review allocations and interactions through dedicated role-based workspaces, including My Allocations , Assigned to Me , Auditor Performance , My Evaluations , Disputes , and Resolved . - Support acknowledgment and dispute workflows for Human Agent evaluations when enabled. - Exclude dispute metrics from AI Agent-only allocations. Note: Dispute-related metrics and statistics don’t apply to allocations that contain only AI Agent conversation segments. ---

title: Audit Allocations
heading: Workspace Views
text: Audit Allocations provides dedicated views for different stages of the audit lifecycle. View Purpose ----------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Allocations Create, manage, and monitor audit allocations. My Allocations View allocations created by the current user. Assigned to Me Access and complete audits assigned to the current user. Auditor Performance Monitor auditor workload, allocation progress, completion rates, average audit scores, and pending audits across the organization. Available only to users with the required permissions. My Evaluations Review evaluations completed by the current user. Disputes Review evaluations pending dispute resolution. Resolved View completed dispute cases and finalized evaluations.

title: Audit Allocations
heading: Access Audit Allocations
text: Navigate to Quality AI AutoQA Allocations . Enable Agent Accept & Dispute in Quality AI Settings Quality AI General Settings to activate the My Evaluations , Disputes , Resolved , and the Review Status column in My Allocations . For steps to create an allocation, see Creating Audit Allocations. For information on managing allocations and auditor views, see Understanding Views and Permissions. ---

title: Conversation Mining
text: Conversation Mining provides supervisors with a centralized workspace to review, analyze, monitor, and audit customer interactions processed by Quality AI. It supports AI Agent, Human Agent, and AI Agent → Human Agent handoff conversations, including processed and pending interactions. For AI Agent → Human Agent handoff interactions, the system represents the AI Agent and Human Agent portions as separate evaluation records. Supervisors can filter, review, audit, and evaluate each record independently. The Handled By field identifies whether a record belongs to an AI Agent or Human Agent segment. Conversation Mining brings together conversation quality, evaluation scores, customer experience, business metadata, sentiment, topics, intents, emotions, resolution outcomes, and operational insights. These insights help supervisors conduct audits, coach agents, investigate issues, and analyze performance across Conversation Mining, AI-Assisted Audit, and Agent Dashboards. Use Contact Direction together with Queue, Experience Flow, Channel, Evaluation Form, and other filters to analyze inbound and outbound interactions. ---

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Contact Direction
text: Use Contact Direction together with Queue, Experience Flow, Channel, Evaluation Form, and other filters to distinguish between Inbound and Outbound interactions. Contact Direction applies to both Human Agent and AI Agent conversations. The available results must respect the selected direction when combined with routing, channel, agent, and evaluation filters. ---

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Interactions Page
text: The Interactions page includes two tabs: - Processed : Displays conversations that have completed Quality AI processing and are available for review, audit, and evaluation. - Pending : Displays conversations awaiting processing or that failed validation. Successfully processed conversations move to the Processed tab. When you enable Agent Accept & Dispute , the Processed tab displays evaluation review status in the Status column and Audit Status filter.

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Key Capabilities
text: - Review processed conversations for coaching, investigations, and quality analysis. - Analyze evaluation scores, sentiment, topics, intents, emotions, and resolution outcomes. - Review AI Agent, Human Agent, and AI-to-Human handoff conversations independently. - Open the corresponding AI or Human audit segment directly from each conversation record. - Identify processing failures independently for versioned AutoQA features, including By Question V1/V2 and By Agent V1/V2, when feature-level processing details are available. - Filter conversations using queues, experience flows, agents, intents, keywords, channels, contact direction, evaluation metrics, and custom fields. - Apply experience filters such as L1, L2, L3 intents, generated intents, resolution status, and duration status. - Customize workspace with configurable columns, saved views, and timeline navigation. - Track review status including agent acknowledgement and dispute status for evaluated conversations. - Maintain V1 and V2 processing statuses independently. A failure in one version doesn’t affect the other. ---

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Conversation Records
text: The conversation type determines the number of rows displayed. Conversation Type Records Displayed ---------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------- Human-only Conversation One Human Agent record. AI-only Conversation One AI Agent record. AI Agent → Human Agent Handoff Two separate records (AI Agent and Human Agent segments). Each record opens its corresponding audit segment. ---

title: Conversation Mining
heading: AI Agent → Human Agent Handoff
text: When an interaction is transferred from an AI Agent to a Human Agent, Conversation Mining creates two separate evaluation records: - AI Agent Record : Represents the AI Agent segment and uses its assigned Experience Flow. - Human Agent Record : Represents the Human Agent segment and uses its assigned Queue. Each segment is evaluated independently. Scores, audit results, metrics, moments, intents, and other segment-specific data remain separate between the two records. ---

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Record Behavior
text: - Each evaluation segment appears as an independent record. - Selecting a Human Agent record opens the Human Agent audit segment. - Selecting an AI Agent record opens the AI Agent audit segment. - AI Agent records use Experience Flow assignments. - Human Agent records use Queue assignments. ---

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Processed Tab
text: The Processed tab (Processed Conversations) displays conversations that have completed Quality AI processing. Select a conversation to open the AI-Assisted Audit screen, where you can review the transcript, evaluation results, sentiment, audit details, and other conversation insights. For AI-to-Human conversations: - Selecting the AI Agent row opens the AI Agent audit segment. - Selecting the Human Agent row opens the Human Agent audit segment.

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Processing Status
text: Indicates the processing status of the conversation and applicable Quality AI features. For AutoQA, processing status is maintained independently for By Question V1 , By Question V2 , By Agent V1 , and By Agent V2 , when configured. Each feature version retains its own processing result. A failure in one version doesn’t overwrite, mask, or change the processing result of another version. For example, a conversation may have a successful By Question V1 result while By Question V2 has failed. The UI must preserve and display these version-specific results independently. The Pending tab is available only when Automation AI, Agent AI, or Contact Center AI (CCAI) conversation sources are enabled for the workspace. ---

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Access Process Tab Conversations
text: Navigate to Quality AI AutoQA Conversation Mining Processing . ---

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Filter by Processing Status
text: Supervisors use the Status filter on the Pending tab to view conversations by processing state. The filter includes the following options: - Select All : Displays all pending conversations regardless of status. - Pending : Displays conversations queued for processing. - In Progress : Displays conversations currently being processed. - Failed : Displays conversations that failed validation. Selecting this option also reveals failure-specific sub-categories. ---

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Conversation Grid Details
text: The Conversation Mining grid displays one record for every evaluation segment. Column Description -------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Handled by Displays whether an AI Agent or Human Agent handles the interaction Assigned to Displays the routing assignment for the interaction as a colored tag. For Human Agent conversations, this displays the assigned Queue. For AI Agent conversations, this displays the assigned Experience Flow. The applicable Queue or Experience Flow determines the evaluation form used for scoring. Agents Displays the name of the agent who last handled and ended the interaction. Processing Status Displays the Quality AI processing state and applicable feature-level processing results, including version-specific AutoQA processing statuses. The system maintains AutoQA feature statuses independently for By Question V1, By Question V2, By Agent V1, and By Agent V2, enabling it to identify failures separately by metric version. Conversation Intelligence generates outputs such as sentiment, topics, intents, and taxonomy-based insights. Actions Displays available actions such as Bookmark and Audit . Conversation Source Platform that ingested the conversation: Automation AI, CCAI, Agent AI, or QM Express (Quality AI Express). Displays after the Actions column. Flow or Queue Displays the assigned Experience Flow for AI Agent conversations or Queue for Human Agent conversations. Kore Evaluation Score Displays the AutoQA evaluation score, when available. Sentiment Score Displays the customer sentiment score derived from the conversation. Supervisor Audit Score Displays the supervisor-assigned score for audited or manually evaluated interact

title: Conversation Mining
heading: AI Agent Conversation Behavior
text: AI Agent conversation segments differ from Human Agent segments. For AI Agent conversations: - Experience Flow replaces Queue. - AI evaluation forms are used. - AI-specific evaluation metrics are used. Speech-related metrics that require Human Agent speech analysis aren’t generated for AI Agent conversations. This includes: Empathy Score, Dead Air, Cross-talk, Speaking Rate, Hold, and Crutch Word Score. These metrics are applicable only to Human Agent conversations. AI Agent conversations mustn’t display or return results for these Human Agent-only metrics. ---

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Pending Tab
text: The Pending tab displays conversations that haven't completed Quality AI processing. This includes conversations in Pending, In Progress, or Failed processing states. - Pending : The conversation is queued and awaiting processing. - In Progress : The conversation is currently being processed. - Failed : The system doesn’t process the conversation successfully because it failed validation or processing. When available, the system displays the failure reason and applicable failure category. Conversations that complete processing successfully are moved to the Processed tab. The Pending tab is available only when Automation AI, Agent AI, or Contact Center AI (CCAI) conversation sources are enabled for the workspace.

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Access Pending Conversations
text: Navigate to Quality AI AutoQA Conversation Mining Pending . Pending Tab Columns Column Description --------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------- Handled By Agent Displays the name of the agent who handled the pending conversation. Conversation ID Displays the conversation identifier for the interaction. Start Date Displays the date when the conversation started. End Date Displays the date when the conversation ended. Processing Status Displays the current state of conversation processing.

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Filter By Processing Status Values
text: Use the Status filter on the Pending tab to filter conversations by processing state. Status or Filter Option Description -------------------------- --------------- Select All Displays all pending conversations. Pending Displays conversations queued for processing. If Scheduled Processing is enabled, conversations remain queued until the next processing window. In Progress Displays conversations that are currently being processed. Failed Indicates that the conversation failed validation and isn't processed. Quality AI records the failure reason and may provide failure-specific categories.

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Filter Conversations
text: Use the toolbar at the top of the Conversation Mining page to locate and manage conversations. Filters are available from the Conversation Mining toolbar and apply to the currently selected Processed or Pending tab. Filter availability and behavior may vary depending on the selected tab and the type of filter. Control Description ----------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Columns Include or exclude specific fields in the Interactions dashboard. Bookmarks Assign interactions to bookmarks and view all bookmarks associated with an interaction. Date and Time Range Select the time range for conversations. The default range is the last 7 days. Filters Open the filter panel to refine the displayed conversations.

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Add New Filter
text: 1. Select Filters from the Conversation Mining toolbar. 2. Select + Add New Filter . 3. Select a filter category. 4. Configure the filter and apply it. The selected filters apply to the active Processed or Pending tab. ---

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Filter Categories
text: The filter panel includes:

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Filter by Efficiency
text: Filter by Efficiency analyzes emotional, behavioral, and qualitative aspects of customer interactions using sentiment, interaction metadata, and operational filters. Handled By Filter conversations based on the type of agent that handled the interaction: - AI Agent : Shows conversations handled by an AI Agent. - Human Agent : Shows conversations handled by a Human Agent. Channels Use this filter to view conversations based on how the interaction took place and its direction. Chat : - Inbound : Shows chat conversations initiated by the customer. - Outbound : Shows chat conversations initiated by an agent or the organization. Voice : - Inbound : Shows voice conversations initiated by the customer, such as incoming calls to an agent or AI Agent. - Outbound : Shows voice conversations initiated by an agent or the organization, such as outgoing calls to a customer. Audit Status Filter conversations based on their audit status: - Assigned : Conversations assigned for audit. - Audited : Conversations that have completed an audit. - Not Assigned : Conversations that aren’t assigned for audit. - Resolved : Conversations with a resolved audit status. - Closed : Conversations with a closed audit status. - Pending Agent Review : Conversations awaiting agent review. - Pending Supervisor Review : Conversations awaiting supervisor review. Audit Allocations Select Audit Allocations to filter and view interactions associated with specific audit batches or allocation groups directly from Conversation Mining without manually filtering individual Conversation IDs. Duration Status Select a Duration Status to control which interactions appear based on evaluation eligibility and duration: Option Description -------- ------------- All (default) Displays all interactions regardless of duration. Evaluated Displays interactions whose duration meets the configured evaluation threshold and for which an evaluation score is generated. Below Threshold Displays interactions whose duration is below

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Filter by Experience
text: This category helps analyze emotional and qualitative aspects of customer interactions using sentiment and emotion-based filters. Filter Description -------- ------------- Avg. Waiting Time Select the average waiting time, in seconds, for the selected date range. Sentiment Trend Analyzes conversation sentiment across different stages using Opening and Closing sentiment options such as Positive, Neutral, Negative, or Any to evaluate customer experience and conversation outcomes. Emotions Helps identify interactions based on detected emotions such as Anger, Fear, Confusion, Sadness, and Happy for targeted emotional and behavioral analysis. Sentiment Score Set the minimum and maximum sentiment range for positive (higher) or negative (lower) sentiment. CSAT Filter by customer satisfaction score to view and drill down into interaction distribution across score ranges based on feedback responses. Configured Intents Filter by topic or intent across L1, L2, L3. Child lists update based on parent selection. Generated Intents Select the AI-generated or configured intents based on your intents. Select Configured Intent levels in order: L1 first, then L2, then L3. You must select at least one level to apply the filter. Overall Resolution Filter by Resolved or Unresolved (both selected by default). The system marks a conversation as resolved when it defines all applicable L3 intents. You can view the CSAT and Avg. Waiting Time filter parameters only when the Connector is in disabled mode.

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Filter by Behavior
text: This category analyzes filters based on agent conduct and interaction dynamics. Filter Description -------- ------------- Metric Name Enables you to select a single evaluation metric (shown as a tag) and filter interactions by Pass or Fail. Manual metrics are visually indicated for audit identification. Metric Qualification Filter interactions by metric outcome. When you select a Dynamic By Question metric in the Metric Name filter, the system enables the following options: - Pass : Trigger detected, and the response matched the expected utterance (Adhered). - Fail : Trigger detected, but the response didn't match the expected utterance (Non-Adhered). Language Select a conversation language to add from the dropdown list. Empathy Score (Human Agent only) Measures how well the agent responds to the customer's emotional state. A higher score indicates a more empathetic interaction. Crutch Word Score (Human Agent only) Measures the use of filler words (for example, um , uh ) by the agent. A higher score indicates greater use of crutch words. Agent Playbook Adherence Displays the Agent AI playbook adherence percentage for an interaction. Kore Evaluation Score Displays the automated QA score for an interaction, based on the evaluation form assigned to an interaction’s queue. Fatal Interactions The system displays interactions that contain fatal issues and excludes them from evaluation scoring. Validation Failure Displays interactions that fail validation and aren't processed for evaluation. You can use Form, Channel, and Language to refine results. Agent Playbook Adherence is available only when a Playbook is configured for the selected form.

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Filter by Keywords
text: This enables you to search, filter, and review conversations using specific keywords or phrases. You can filter by included or excluded keywords and by speaker, with results linked directly to the QA audit screen. Category Details ---------- --------- Filter by Keywords Helps you search, filter, and review conversations using specific keywords or phrases. Supports included/excluded keywords and speaker-based filtering, with results linked directly to the QA audit screen. Conditions (AND / OR) Select how the system evaluates multiple included keywords. - AND : All specified keywords must appear in the conversation. For example: Include Billing AND frustrated (both speakers) and Exclude Resolved (both speakers). - OR : At least one keyword must display. For example, include Refund OR Money Back (customer only) and Exclude Processed (agent only), and Completed (both speakers). Conversation Including Keywords Add keywords to include conversations in results. Select a speaker ( Agent only , Customer only , or Both ) and use + Add Keyword to include up to 8 keywords. Conversation Excluding Keywords Add keywords to exclude conversations from results. Select speaker scope ( Agent only , Customer only , or Both ) and use + Add Exclude Keyword to add up to 5 exclusions. All exclusions follow AND NOT logic. Audit Navigation and Filtering Enables quick filtering and navigation by keyword or QA question, with auto-scrolling of transcripts and relevance-based matching. Apply Keywords Action Applies the selected include or exclude keyword filters and updates results. ---

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Filter by Custom Fields
text: This helps to refine interactions using business-specific metadata from Express File or Agent AI integrations. Custom fields are dynamically available based on the selected date range. The system excludes interactions that doesn't include the selected field from results. To apply a custom field filter: 1. Select Custom Fields from the Filter By panel. 1. Select the Key from the dropdown. For example: Account ID . 1. Enter the matching Value . 1. (Optional) Select + Add Custom Field to include additional key-value pairs. 1. Select Apply or Save & Apply . Conversations that don't carry the selected custom field are excluded from results entirely. Filtered Keywords Interactions Displays the count of interactions matching the selected keywords (for example, Filtered Interactions: 22 ).

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Connector-Dependent Filters
text: The availability of certain filters depends on the Connector configuration. When Quality AI Express is disabled under Conversation Sources, the following filters are disabled: - By Experience : Avg. Waiting Time, AHT, and No. of Transfers - By Efficiency : CSAT and Avg. Waiting Time When Quality AI Express is enabled, these filters are available when supported by the Connector configuration. The system automatically disables filters that the current Connector configuration doesn’t support, so you can’t apply them. ---

title: Conversation Mining
heading: Manage Saved Filters
text: Use the Saved Filters UI to apply, store, and manage filter configurations on the Conversation Mining dashboard. Action Description -------- ------------- Apply Filters Stores current settings as an Unsaved Filter. Save & Apply Saves and names filters for audit allocation. Saving is optional if audits aren't used. Save Filters Saves the current filter configuration with a name and optionally sets it as the default on the Interactions dashboard. View Saved Filters Shows all saved and unsaved filters. Filtered Interactions Displays a real-time count of matching conversations. Customization Options Includes Copy, Mark as Default, Edit, and Delete filters. If interactions aren't used for audit allocation, you can apply the current filters without saving them as a reusable saved filter.

title: Creating Audit Allocations
text: Creating Audit Allocations provides a guided workflow to configure audit allocations by defining the evaluation scope, selecting interactions, assigning auditors, and configuring dispute handling when applicable. During the workflow, select the evaluation form, date range, languages, and applicable queues, agents, or agent groups, then choose a Random or Custom allocation method to determine which interactions are included for evaluation. The workflow dynamically displays only the configuration options applicable to the selected evaluation form and provides a real-time summary of the selected interactions before you create the allocation. For a feature summary, refer to Audit Allocations Overview. For role-based access and view details, refer to Understanding Views and Permissions.

title: Creating Audit Allocations
heading: Access Audit Allocations
text: Navigate to Quality AI AutoQA Allocations New Audit Allocation . ---

title: Creating Audit Allocations
heading: Evaluation Form Types
text: The selected evaluation form determines which conversations are included in an allocation. For Automation AI conversations, the evaluation form is assigned to the corresponding Experience Flow. While the allocation workflow is the same for all evaluation form types, the available allocation scope and assignment options depend on the selected form and its configuration. Evaluation Form Type Evaluates Allocation Behavior ---------------------------- -------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Human Agent Human agent conversations Uses queue-based allocations. Supports assignment by Agent , Agent Group , or Queue based on the selected queues. AI Agent (Automation AI) Automation AI conversations Uses the evaluation form assigned to the corresponding Experience Flow . Supports allocations for AI Agent conversations based on the configured Experience Flows. Hybrid Human agent and AI Agent conversations Supports allocations for both conversation types using the assignment scope defined in the evaluation form configuration. The allocation workflow (Settings → Allocation → Assignment) is consistent across all evaluation form types. The available queues, Experience Flows, and assignment options vary based on the available queues, Experience Flows, and assignment options vary based on the selected evaluation form and its configuration. ---

title: Creating Audit Allocations
heading: Before You Begin
text: Before creating an allocation: - Create and activate an evaluation form. - Assign the evaluation form to the appropriate queue or Experience Flow. - Confirm auditors have the required permissions. - Confirm eligible interactions exist for the selected evaluation period. ---

title: Creating Audit Allocations
heading: Create a New Allocation
text: Navigate to Quality AI AutoQA Allocations New Allocation . ---

title: Creating Audit Allocations
heading: Step 1: Settings
text: Configure the allocation details and define the interactions to include in the audit. The available Settings fields vary depending on the selected evaluation form. For AI Agent (Automation AI) evaluation forms, the system displays options applicable to AI Agent conversations instead of the queue- and agent-based options shown for Human Agent evaluation forms. Configure Basic Information 1. Select New Allocation to open the allocation wizard. 1. Enter a unique Name for the allocation. 1. (Optional) Enter a Description to identify the allocation. 1. Select the Date Range from which the system retrieves eligible interactions. 1. Select an Evaluation Form . The selected evaluation form determines the available languages, queues or Experience Flows, agents, and other allocation options. 1. Select one or more Languages to limit the allocation to interactions in those languages. The available languages depend on the selected evaluation form. 1. Select one or more Queues associated with the selected evaluation form. This field is available for Human Agent evaluation forms. 1. (Optional) Select one or more Agents to include in the allocation. Leave this field blank to include all agents in the selected queues. Users with Cross Queue Data Access can search across all queues. This field is available for Human Agent evaluation forms. 1. (Optional) Select one or more Agent Groups to include in the allocation. This field is available for Human Agent evaluation forms. 1. Select Next to proceed to the Allocation step. The fields displayed in the Settings step depend on the selected evaluation form. For Automation AI evaluation forms, the system displays Experience Flow instead of Queue , Agents , and Agent Groups . The interaction counts update automatically as you modify the filters. ---

title: Creating Audit Allocations
heading: Step 2: Allocation Type
text: Choose how the system selects interactions from the filtered dataset for audit.

title: Creating Audit Allocations
heading: Allocation Type
text: Select the allocation type to determine how the system selects interactions for the audit. Allocation Type Description ------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Random Selects interactions automatically based on the configured allocation method and sampling criteria. Custom Selects interactions using a saved filter or by including all interactions that match the selected criteria. Random Allocation When you select Random , configure the following options: 1. Select a Channel Type : Voice , Chat , and Both . This Setting is configurable independently for Voice and Chat channels, enabling flexible allocation behavior across different interaction types. 1. (Optional) Turn on Include interactions below duration threshold to include interactions below the configured duration threshold. - Off (default): The system excludes Below Threshold and Duration Unavailable contacts from the random draw pool. - On : Flagged contacts become eligible for selection alongside evaluated contacts, so QA teams can spot-review incomplete interactions as part of the audit cycle. 1. Configure separate allocation logic for Voice and Chat interactions. Logic Description ------- ------------- Percentage Per Agent Allocate a percentage of each agent's interactions and for each enabled channel. Interactions Per Agent Allocate a fixed number of interactions per agent and for each enabled channel. 1. Enter the required percentage or interaction count for each enabled channel. 1. Review the Selected interactions for audit summary. The system automatically updates the Total Selected Interactions , Voice Interactions , and Chat Interactions counts based on the allocation settings. 1. Select Next to proceed to the Assignment step. Custom Allocation When you select Custom , configure the following options: 1. Select a Save Filters source. Saved Filter : Select a filter previously saved in Conversation Mining. Best for recurr

title: Creating Audit Allocations
heading: Step 3: Assignment
text: Distribute selected interactions across the auditor team, ensuring balanced workload and activating the allocation for evaluation. 1. Use the Search Auditors dropdown to select team members who evaluate interactions. 2. Choose multiple auditors to distribute the workload. Consider these factors when selecting auditors. 3. Enter the Allocation Percentage for each auditor. The system calculates the exact interaction count per auditor automatically. 4. Review the Interactions column, which automatically calculates the exact interaction count for each auditor based on your percentage input. Example (100 total interactions, 3 auditors): - Auditor A: 40% = 40 interactions - Auditor B: 30% = 30 interactions - Auditor C: 30% = 30 interactions 5. Verify that the total equals 100%. 6. Review your complete allocation configuration: - Settings : Form, languages, agents, agent groups. - Allocation : Method (Random or Custom), filters, total interactions. - Assignment : Auditors and their percentages. 7. Select Save to activate the allocation. When activated, the system immediately assigns interactions to auditors. Auditors can see their assignments in the Assigned to Me tab right away. After Creating an Allocation - The allocation displays in your My Allocations tab. - Auditors see their assigned interactions in Assigned to Me . - Track completion progress in real-time. - AI Agent evaluations are processed as system-scoped evaluation sets. - Edit the allocation at any time to reassign pending interactions. - You can reassign the pending interactions at any time without affecting completed evaluations. The system automatically calculates the interaction count for each auditor and enables Save only when the allocation totals 100%. If you enable Agent Accept & Dispute and configure disputes for the selected evaluation form, the Review Status column tracks agent acknowledgments and dispute activity for all audited interactions in the allocation. ---

title: Creating Audit Allocations
heading: Step 4: Dispute Allocation (Human Agent Only)
text: Available only when Agent Accept & Dispute is enabled. Dispute Resolution Assignment The Dispute Resolution Assignment setting to enable or disable disputes feature for evaluations under this allocation. State Behavior ------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ On Enable agents to acknowledge or dispute metric-level scores for evaluations under this allocation. Off Prevent agents from responding to evaluations. The system hides the Accept and Dispute options and marks evaluations as Audited upon completion. Dispute Routing Rule When you enable Dispute Resolution Assignment , select how the system routes disputes for re-evaluation. Option Description --------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------- Same Auditor Route disputes to the auditor who performed the original evaluation. Different Auditor Route disputes to a different auditor selected from the auditor list. Auditor List (Different Auditor Only) When you select Different Auditor , define the pool of auditors available for dispute routing. Add Auditors - Select Search Auditors to Add . - Search for and select one or more auditors. - Select Add . Added auditors display in the list below the search field. If you don't add any auditors, the system shows No Auditors Added . Allow Multi-Round Re-Disputes The Allow Multi-Round Re-Disputes option controls whether agents can raise additional disputes after QA re-evaluation. State Behavior ------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- On Enable agents to dispute QA re-evaluations and initiate additional rounds up to the configured limit. Off Make the QA decision final. The system prevents further disputes and shows an in-context message to agents. Maximum Re-Disputes Allowed When you enable multi-round disputes, select the maximum number o

title: Creating Audit Allocations
heading: Use Case Example: Redistribute Pending Audits
text: Scenario : A QA Manager creates a monthly random sample allocation for 15 auditors. Three days later, two auditors report unexpected leave, leaving 40 pending interactions unassigned.

title: Creating Audit Allocations
heading: Scenario
text: A QA Manager creates a monthly audit allocation for multiple auditors. During the audit cycle, two auditors become unavailable, leaving several pending interactions unreviewed.

title: Creating Audit Allocations
heading: Resolution
text: The QA Manager edits the allocation, selects the unavailable auditors, and reassigns their pending interactions to available auditors by updating the workload distribution. The system redistributes only the pending interactions, while completed evaluations remain unchanged. Newly assigned auditors immediately see the reassigned interactions in Assigned to Me.

title: Creating Audit Allocations
heading: Outcome
text: The system keeps the monthly audit on schedule, prevents loss or duplication of interactions, and balances workload across available team members. ---

title: Customer Experience Insights
text: Customer Experience (CX) Insights provides a unified post-interaction view of customer experience across conversations, queues, channels, and contact directions. It helps supervisors, QA managers, and CX leaders analyze customer satisfaction, sentiment, resolution outcomes, churn risk, and key satisfaction drivers using real conversation data. The Handled By filter is available across all CX Insights views, including Sentiment Distribution , Customer Churn Monitor , CSAT Drivers , DSAT Drivers , and Insights Mining , enabling users to analyze interactions handled by AI Agents, Human Agents, or both. Users with Cross Queue Data Access can view and filter data across all queues. Whereas, other users can access only their assigned queues. The Channel filter supports direction-aware analysis by displaying interactions that match the selected Inbound , Outbound , or Both contact direction.

title: Customer Experience Insights
heading: Why Use CX Insights?
text: Use Case How CX Insights Helps -------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Experience Monitoring Tracks resolution, wait time, and customer sentiment trends. AI Agent and Human Agent Analysis Analyze customer experience separately for AI Agent, Human Agent, or both using the Handled By filter.
